product-widget.purpose: Draws one of the **official console widgets**: a scaled, inert mock of an Azion Console screen or fragment, built from real webkit components inside a `shell-mockup` frame, that marketing bands use to show the product. `name` selects the widget from a closed registry of 70 drawings, loaded on demand, so a page can only render mocks that already exist and the same screen is the same drawing on every page that shows it. The remaining props pass through to the widget that declares them, and a widget that does not declare one keeps its own value.

The same console screen appears on more than one page and must be the same drawing on each.
Several widgets share one slot (tabs), and only the one showing should play: drive `active` from the host.
A grid cell plays its fragment's beat while the pointer is over it: drive `hover` from the host.

A screenshot or clip in documentation → use `doc-frame`.

illustration` — the same closed-registry pattern for static scenes.

shell-mockup.purpose: A scaled, inert picture of an Azion Console screen, for marketing bands that show the product. The consumer composes the screen's body from real webkit components at a fixed design width; the frame draws the console shell around it (the slim console bar, the side rail with breadcrumbs and actions, or the previous console's top bar) and scales the whole drawing to fit its host. Each piece of the body is a `ShellMockup.Part` that travels in on its own beat once the mockup scrolls into view, so the screen assembles itself instead of appearing all at once.
useWhen: Showing a console screen or fragment on a marketing band: a hero, a media split, a feature tab, a widget grid cell.
Depicting a product workflow with real webkit controls instead of a screenshot, so the drawing follows the theme and stays sharp at any size.
Staggering the parts of a mock so they arrive in reading order when the band scrolls into view, and replaying that entrance each time a tab makes the mock active.
Drawing only a fragment of a screen (a list, a form row) floating on the band's own surface, with `kind="bare"` and `chrome` off.
avoidWhen: To show a real, working screen at a device size → use `browser-frame`; it renders live content in a true viewport, not a scaled picture.
For a static screenshot or clip in documentation → use `doc-frame`.
For an illustration scene → use `illustration`.
related: browser-frame` — a live, resizable viewport for real screens; `shell-mockup` is an inert, scaled drawing of the console.
texture-material` — the texture the frame grounds itself with when `texture` is set.
frame-box` — the page's registration frame a mockup band is often placed inside.
bestPractices: Compose the body at the design width (`width`, `mobileWidth`), not at the host's width; the frame scales the drawing, so sizes inside are design pixels.
Give the host a height (or an aspect ratio); the frame fills its host and derives its design height from it.
Number parts in reading order with `order`, starting at `0`; parts on the same beat land together.
Keep the mockup decorative: it is hidden from assistive technology unless `interactive` is set, so the band's own copy must say what the picture shows.
Set `active` from the host when several mockups share one slot (tabs), so only the visible one plays and it replays when it returns.
Tune a fade with the consumer-side custom properties `--mockup-fade-start` / `--mockup-fade-end` (or `--mockup-fade-edge` for `y`) and match its color to the host surface with `--mockup-fade-color`.

props.name: meta
props.doc: Prepend the meta/command modifier glyph (⌘ on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere).

props.name: ctrl
props.doc: Prepend the Control modifier glyph (⌃ on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere).

props.name: shift
props.doc: Prepend the Shift modifier glyph (⇧).

props.name: alt
props.doc: Prepend the Alt/Option modifier glyph (⌥ on macOS, Alt elsewhere).

props.name: size
props.doc: Size token; `small` is a denser keycap for menus, command bars, and table cells.

props.name: keyName
props.doc: Named key printed from the locale catalog (`escape` → `Esc`, `enter` → `Enter`); the slot still renders after it.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The single key or glyph rendered after any modifier glyphs (`K`, `Enter`, `Esc`).

kbd.purpose: Kbd renders keyboard input — a single key or a shortcut combination — as a compact, non-interactive keycap. It reads like a real key: a bordered surface with a thicker bottom edge for depth. Modifier keys are passed as boolean props (`meta`, `shift`, `alt`, `ctrl`) and rendered with the correct OS-aware glyph (⌘ on macOS, the catalog's `Ctrl` elsewhere), and named keys (`keyName`) print their localized name, so consumers never hardcode platform symbols or English key names. Use it for shortcut hints in prose, menus, and control suffixes (e.g. the ⌘K hint in `command`).
useWhen: Show a keyboard shortcut or a single key inline (a ⌘K hint on a search button, an `Esc` hint in a dialog, `/` to focus search).
Present a modifier combination whose glyph should adapt to the user's OS.
avoidWhen: The token is a status/category label, not a key → use `tag` or `badge`.
You need an interactive control that fires on click → use `button` / `icon-button`; Kbd is a presentational hint only.
related: command` — consumes Kbd for its per-item shortcut hints and its ⌘K trigger affordance.
badge` — compact non-interactive indicator for counts/status; Kbd is specifically for keyboard keys.
bestPractices: Keep the default slot to a single key or glyph (`K`, `7`, `Enter`, `Esc`, `/`); avoid lowercase words or sentences.
Pass modifiers as boolean props rather than hardcoding `⌘`/`⇧` so the glyph adapts to the OS.

Name a key with `key-name` (`<Kbd key-name="escape" />`) instead of typing `Esc` or `Enter`: the text comes from the locale catalog (`kbd.*`), so it follows `WebkitProvider` (`Espaço` in pt-BR, `Intro` in es) and a consumer renames it with `messages` (`{ kbd: { ctrl: 'Strg' } }`). The macOS symbols `⌘`, `⌃`, `⌥` and `⇧` are never translated.
Place surrounding punctuation outside the element, not inside the keycap.

props.name: columns
props.doc: Columns at full width; fewer columns when a cell would get narrower than `--container-3xs`.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Replaces every value with a skeleton while the data loads; labels stay visible.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the list when no visible heading names it.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: KeyValuePairs.Item` children, or `KeyValuePairs.Group` children — one shape per instance.

key-value-pairs.purpose: A grid of labelled facts about one subject: each pair is a key (the term) and its value, which may be plain text or a composed component such as a `Link`, `Tag`, `CopyButton` or `StatusIndicator`. It renders a native description list laid out in 1 to 4 responsive columns, optionally split into titled groups, and owns its loading and empty-value surfaces. It replaces the hand-rolled label/value grids the resource detail templates (`ResourceSummary`, the detail Overview tabs) draw today.
useWhen: The facts band of a resource detail or Overview page: ID, status, region, created at, domain.
A read-only summary of settings before a confirm step (review step, deploy summary).
Any set of named attributes of a single subject where the reader scans keys to find a value.
Facts that fall into named clusters (General, Networking, Source) shown side by side as titled columns.
avoidWhen: Rows of many subjects compared attribute by attribute → use `table`.
Editable fields → use the form field components (`field` with `input`, `select`, …); this component is read-only.
A single headline figure with a trend → use `stat-tile`.
A list of items with no key/value relation → use a plain list or `item`.
related: table` — many subjects, one row each; KeyValuePairs describes one subject.
card` — the surface a KeyValuePairs usually sits in; KeyValuePairs brings no surface of its own.
copy-button` — the trailing copy affordance for IDs and keys inside a value.
status-indicator`, `tag` — status and category values.
link` — a value that navigates (a domain, a linked resource).
hint` — the info glyph composed into an Item's `info` slot.
skeleton` — rendered in place of each value while the root is `loading`.
bestPractices: Keep keys short nouns in sentence case ("Created", "Region"), never sentences or trailing colons.
Order pairs by what the reader looks for first: identity, status, then the rest.
Use `columns` for width, not for grouping; use `KeyValuePairs.Group` when the facts form named clusters, one group per column.
Do not mix bare Items and Groups at the same level; pick one shape per instance.
Leave the value slot out (or render nothing in it) when a value is absent; the component shows the em dash and its accessible "Not set". Do not type your own "-", "N/A" or "None".
Put a `CopyButton` after an ID or key, never in place of the visible value.
Use the `info` slot for a short `Hint` that explains the key; long explanations belong in the page, not in a tooltip.
Drive `loading` from the data request so the labels stay in place and only the values shimmer.

Editable fields → use the form field components (`field` with `input`, `select`, …); this component is read-only.
A single headline figure with a trend → use `stat-tile`.
A list of items with no key/value relation → use a plain list or `item`.
related: table` — many subjects, one row each; KeyValuePairs describes one subject.
card` — the surface a KeyValuePairs usually sits in; KeyValuePairs brings no surface of its own.
copy-button` — the trailing copy affordance for IDs and keys inside a value.
status-indicator`, `tag` — status and category values.
link` — a value that navigates (a domain, a linked resource).
hint` — the info glyph composed into an Item's `info` slot.
skeleton` — rendered in place of each value while the root is `loading`.
bestPractices: Keep keys short nouns in sentence case ("Created", "Region"), never sentences or trailing colons.
Order pairs by what the reader looks for first: identity, status, then the rest.
Use `columns` for width, not for grouping; use `KeyValuePairs.Group` when the facts form named clusters, one group per column.
Do not mix bare Items and Groups at the same level; pick one shape per instance.
Leave the value slot out (or render nothing in it) when a value is absent; the component shows the em dash and its accessible "Not set". Do not type your own "-", "N/A" or "None".
Put a `CopyButton` after an ID or key, never in place of the visible value.
Use the `info` slot for a short `Hint` that explains the key; long explanations belong in the page, not in a tooltip.
Drive `loading` from the data request so the labels stay in place and only the values shimmer.

props.name: region
props.doc: Which part of the world has its PoPs lit; the map always frames the whole world.

props.name: density
props.doc: How many PoPs are lit, from `none` to `high`.

props.name: animated
props.doc: Pulses the PoPs in three staggered waves; static when false.

props.name: opacity
props.doc: Opacity of the landmass dots, from 0 to 1; the PoPs stay at full strength.

props.name: position
props.doc: Where the map parks in the space the box leaves over.

props.name: scale
props.doc: Size of the map relative to the box; 1 fits it, below 1 shrinks it toward its position, above 1 enlarges it.

props.name: offsetX
props.doc: Horizontal shift as a fraction of the map width; negative moves it left, positive right, past the box edge if large enough.

props.name: offsetY
props.doc: Vertical shift as a fraction of the map height; negative moves it up, positive down, past the box edge if large enough.

props.name: fade
props.doc: Fades the map out along an axis so it meets content without a hard edge.

network-map.purpose: A decorative, full-bleed layer that paints the dotted world map with Azion's PoPs lit in the brand accent. It is a material — it takes no content and claims no space — but unlike a static illustration it is tuned by the consumer (region, PoP density, landmass opacity, static or animated) to sit behind a band's copy.
useWhen: As the backdrop of a band whose subject is the network (reach, data centers, latency, resilience), composed as a sibling under the band's copy inside a positioned, clipping ancestor.
When a band is about one part of the network, so only that region's PoPs should light (`region`) while the whole world stays drawn.
When the same artwork has to read with more or fewer PoPs lit, or with none at all (`density="none"`), from one component instead of separate exports.
avoidWhen: For a real node/edge diagram driven by data → use `flow`.
As a wrapper around content. The layer is absolutely positioned and paints only itself; content is a sibling above it.
related: frame-box` — the ruled box a network band usually sits in; it supplies the positioned, clipping ancestor.
bestPractices: Give the layer a positioned ancestor (`relative overflow-hidden`); it fills that box and nothing else.

Never offset or resize the layer with utilities (`left-*`, `w-*`, `inset-*`). It always fills its positioned ancestor, and `position` + `fade` place the map inside that box — so a fade measures from the band's own edges. An offset box moves the fade's edges off the band's and makes the two placements fight.

To make the map smaller or larger inside its box, set `scale` instead of resizing the layer. The map shrinks toward its `position` corner, so there is no hard edge and the fade keeps measuring from the band's edges.
Keep `opacity` low (the default `0.4`) when copy sits over the landmass; the PoPs keep full strength so the network still reads.
For copy on one side of a band, park the map on the other side with `position` and fade it toward the copy (`position="right"` + `fade="left"`); the default stops need no consumer class.
Tune where a fade holds and ends with `--network-map-fade-start` / `--network-map-fade-end` only when the default stops do not fit, instead of adding masks.
Leave `animated` off by default; turn it on for the one band per page whose subject is the network.
To nudge the map or let it run off the band, set `offsetX` / `offsetY` (for example `:offset-x="0.15"` to bleed right, `:offset-y="-0.1"` to bleed up) instead of offsetting the layer.
asia` and `oceania` hold no PoPs — the artwork carries no accent field there — so either region lights none and the map reads as landmass alone.

props.name: copyable

log-view.purpose: Composition-based terminal log viewer for CI/deploy output. **LogView** is the root shell and context provider; **LogViewHeader**, **LogViewContent**, and **LogViewFooter** are composed as children so teams can reorder, omit, or replace the toolbar and footer without forking the log renderer.
useWhen: Showing build, deploy or CI output as timestamped lines the reader can search, filter to warnings, and copy.
A log shell whose toolbar and footer vary by screen — compose `LogViewHeader`, `LogViewContent` and `LogViewFooter` in the order you need, or drop the ones you don't.
A log that is still loading from the server — set `loading` to show a spinner and `loading-label` in place of the body.
avoidWhen: Static, read-only code or configuration snippets → use `code-block`.
An animated terminal session on a marketing page → use `cli-terminal`.
Rows of structured records with columns, sorting or paging → use `table`.
related: code-block` — highlighted source code with a copy action, not a stream of typed log lines.
cli-terminal` — marketing band that plays a scripted terminal session.
deploy-success` — the post-deploy screen that embeds `log-view` for the build log.
bestPractices: Give every line a stable `id` and a `type` (`text`, `folder`, `framework-version`, `success`, `warning`); the type drives the line's rendering and the warnings filter.
Bind `v-model:search` and `v-model:warnings-only` when the app needs the filter state; otherwise leave them unbound and the header manages them.
Set `:bordered="false"` when the log sits inside a surface that already frames it (an accordion panel, a drawer).
The copy control hides while `disabled` or `loading`, or when there is nothing to copy; listen to `@copy` for the copied text instead of reading the clipboard.
Use the header's `left` / `right` / `search` slots and the footer's default slot to add actions, rather than rebuilding the toolbar.

props.name: copyable

props.name: animateLines

props.name: bordered

code-block.purpose: Read-only code viewer for docs, API examples, and configuration previews. Supports four Figma-documented layouts that share one monolithic shell: 1. **Language switcher** ([4567:33761](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-33761)) — tabbed snippets with a sliding pill, optional filename bar, syntax highlighting, and copy. 2. **Show filename** ([4567:30198](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-30198)) — single snippet with a raised filename bar (language icon + name), no tabs. 3. **Diff** ([4567:29012](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-29012)) — per-line added/removed markers (`+`/`-`), semantic row backgrounds, and a 2 px leading bar; no tabs or filename bar. 4. **Highlighted line** ([4567:31473](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-31473)) — one active line with info background and leading bar; no tabs or filename bar. Regions render conditionally from tab data — the consumer does not pick a separate `kind`. Tab header appears when `tabs.length > 1`. Filename bar appears when the active tab sets `fileName`. Diff and highlight decorations come from `lineChanges` and `highlightedLine` on the active tab. **Syntax highlighting** is driven by the active tab's `language` and resolves to one of these tokenisers, all of which emit the same seven token types (`keyword`, `string`, `function`, `type`, `punctuation`, `identifier`, `comment`) so every language shares the one `--code-sintax-*` palette:
useWhen: Read-only code in docs, API examples or configuration previews that readers copy from.
The same snippet in several languages, switched by tabs (one `tabs` entry per language).
Showing a change as a diff (`lineChanges`) or pointing at one line (`highlightedLine`) on the active tab.
avoidWhen: The content is build or deploy output with timestamps and log levels → use `log-view`.
It is a marketing band that pairs a claim with its code → use `code-split`, or `sticky-scroll-code` for several claims.
It is a terminal session of CLI commands on a product page → use `cli-terminal`.
You only need to copy one short value (a token, an ID) without showing a block → use `copy-button`.
related: copy-button` — the copy control CodeBlock embeds; use it alone for one-line values.
log-view` — terminal-style viewer for CI and deploy logs.
code-split` — page section built around one code sample.
scroll-area` — the scroll container the code region runs in.
bestPractices: Put the source on each tab's `code`. There is no top-level `code` prop, and a tab without a `value` or a `code` is dropped.
Set `language` on every tab. Only JavaScript/TypeScript, shell, HCL, GraphQL and Markdown are tokenised; anything else renders as flat text.
Use `default-value` for the initial tab, and `v-model` only when something outside the block must follow the selected tab.
Set `:copyable="false"` on decorative blocks, and `:bordered="false"` when the block sits inside a surface that already frames it.
Keep `animate-lines` for marketing layouts; leave it off in docs and console screens.

props.name: maxHeight
props.doc: Max height (CSS length). The viewport scrolls dynamically: horizontal scroll appears automatically when columns overflow the width; vertical scroll appears only when `maxHeight` is set smaller than the content (under the sticky header).

props.name: bordered
props.doc: Draw the outer card border around the table. Off by default (the table is typically framed by a surrounding surface); set `bordered` / `:bordered="…"` to draw the `var(--border-default)` outline. The internal row dividers are unaffected.

props.name: data
props.doc: Data-driven mode: row records.

props.name: columns
props.doc: Data-driven mode: column definitions (`{ id?, accessorKey?, header?, label?, enableSorting?, grow?, principal?, frozen?, width?, minWidth?, align?, kind?, resizable?, hideable?, orderable? }`; `width` (px) sets a fixed pixel column (also needed when a frozen column precedes another frozen column on the same edge, so sticky offsets can be summed); **`minWidth`** (px) sets a **floor** instead: the table measures the column's own content — its header, including the sort affordance, and every rendered body cell — and pins the column to the larger of the two, as **one** width applied to the header and every body cell (a per-cell `min-width` would let each row size to its own content and drift the header away from the body). It is for a column whose content is a chip or a short token: a fixed `width` there is a bet in both directions — too generous and it reserves space the rest of the row needs, too tight and the chip inside it truncates. The measured width tracks the **rendered page**, so a column can change width when paging or sorting brings longer content into view; `width` wins when both are set, and a user resize wins over both. a `grow` column without `width` keeps a shared fixed basis so the header and body stay aligned and the cell never wraps. A column with no `grow` defaults to weight `2` for the **principal** column and `1` for the rest, so the columns fill the available space proportionally. The principal column is the one flagged `principal: true`, or — when none is flagged — the first non-action column. A `kind: 'action'` column is automatically pinned to the trailing (right) edge — staying reachable while the rest scrolls horizontally — and is never resizable. **`resizable: true`** opts a column into a live mouse/touch drag-to-resize handle on its header (native pointer events; the `@tanstack/vue-table` exception covers sorting/pagination/selection/visibility, not sizing). On the first drag of any divider every flexible column freezes at its current rendered width; from then on dragging changes **only that column** and the table grows (horizontal scroll) — the others are untouched. The drag floor is the column's own content width (header label + visible body cells), so a column never shrinks past its content. Frozen and action columns ignore `resizable`. **`label`** overrides the `Table.ColumnSelector` label when `header` is not a string; **`hideable: false`** excludes the column from `Table.ColumnSelector` (e.g. the actions column); **`orderable: true`** opts the column into `columnOrder`. When non-empty, the table renders itself via TanStack.

props.name: rowsPerPageOptions

props.name: loading
props.doc: Data-driven mode: render skeleton rows in the body (aligned to the visible columns) and set `aria-busy`; `Table.RefreshButton` disables/spins while true. Precedence: `loading` → skeleton, else rows, else `empty`.

props.name: filters
props.doc: v-model:filters — structured applied conditions committed by `Table.Filter`, distinct from `globalFilter`. Client-side they map to TanStack column filters; under `manualFiltering` they are emitted for a server refetch.

props.name: filterFields
props.doc: Field catalog the built-in `Table.Filter` builder offers (id, label, value type, allowed operators, select options). Omit and use `Table.Filter`'s default slot to plug a custom builder.

props.name: state
props.doc: v-model:state — an aggregate serializable snapshot layered over the per-concern models. A bound per-concern v-model (e.g. `v-model:sorting`) wins over `state` for that concern.

props.name: initialState
props.doc: Uncontrolled seed applied once on mount; seeds only concerns that are not bound to their own v-model.

props.name: exportRows
props.doc: Rows `Table.Export` and `exportCsv()` write for the `filtered` and `all` scopes in place of the rows the table holds (the `page` scope always writes the rendered page). `useCollection` binds it so an export covers every match, not only the page; a promise is awaited before the `export` event and the download.

props.name: exportFilename

props.name: stackable
props.doc: Data-driven mode: when the table's own box is narrower than `--container-lg`, each row renders as a card of label and value pairs instead of a horizontally scrolling grid. Set false to keep the grid at every width.

props.name: wrapLines
props.doc: Data-driven mode: cell text wraps onto several lines instead of truncating.

props.name: striped
props.doc: Data-driven mode: every other body row takes the raised surface.

props.name: density
props.doc: Row density: `compact` shrinks body rows and cell padding.

props.name: virtual
props.doc: Data-driven mode: render only the rows in view, for thousands of rows. The viewport scrolls vertically within `maxHeight` (40rem when empty). Ignored in the stacked layout.

props.name: estimateRowHeight
props.doc: Row height (px) assumed in `virtual` mode until a row is measured.

slots.name: toolbar

slots.name: filters
slots.notes: Active-filter chips row below the toolbar (both modes); same scope as `toolbar`.

slots.name: empty
slots.notes: Data-driven mode: shown when there are no rows. Defaults to an empty-state block (illustration + title + description) following Figma; override the slot for custom copy/actions.

table.purpose: Composition primitives for building accessible, pixel-perfect data tables, in two modes. **Composition mode** (default): compose the anatomy by hand (header / body / rows / cells) — the component owns markup, tokens, a11y, configurable column sizing (an emphasized first column), sortable headers, selectable rows, and a **freeze system** for sticky columns (e.g. an actions column) and a sticky header. **Data-driven mode**: pass `data` + `columns` and the table renders itself via the headless **`@tanstack/vue-table`** engine, still rendering through the same primitives (our markup/tokens/a11y, pixel-perfect to Figma). Pairs with the [`Pagination`](./pagination.md) component (rendered automatically in the footer when `paginated`). A top **toolbar band** (`title` / `toolbar` / `filters` slots) sits above the scroll viewport in both modes for a title, search / filter / export / column-selector actions, and removable filter chips; the `toolbar` and `filters` slots are scoped with the TanStack `table` instance (in data-driven mode) so the consumer can drive filtering, global search, and column visibility through the table's own methods. **Engine.** Data-driven mode is driven by **`@tanstack/vue-table`** (`useVueTable` + `getCoreRowModel` / `getSortedRowModel` / `getFilteredRowModel` / `getPaginationRowModel`), covering sorting, pagination, row selection, column visibility, and global filtering — client- and server-side (`manualSorting` / `manualPagination` / `manualFiltering`). It is a pure-logic library (no markup/styles/positioning/animation), granted narrowly to this single component per [`.claude/rules/dependencies.md`](../.claude/rules/dependencies.md) § Exceptions; rendering stays 100% in our primitives. State is exposed via v-model (`sorting`, `rowSelection`, `columnVisibility`, `globalFilter`, `pagination`, plus the structured `filters` model and the aggregate `state` snapshot below). `@tanstack/virtual` remains forbidden: the opt-in `virtual` mode windows the rows itself (spacer padding above and below the rendered slice, sized from a height index: each rendered row is measured with a `ResizeObserver`, rows not yet rendered take the average of the first rows measured, and when a row above the rows in view changes height the scroll position moves by the same amount so the rows in view stay still). Without `virtual`, a list of more than 200 rows renders its first 50 rows and mounts the rest as a spacer below them nears the viewport (an `IntersectionObserver`), so a long page costs what is on screen. **Toolbar & imperative API.** The toolbar band composes context-aware controls that drive the table through the injected context with no wiring: `Table.Filter` (a structured field/operator/value builder that commits removable/editable filter chips, with an escape slot to plug a custom builder such as the console's AQL), `Table.AppliedFilters` (the chips), `Table.ColumnSelector` (a column-visibility picker over the existing `columnVisibility` state), `Table.Export` (CSV download), and `Table.RefreshButton`. Structured filters are a first-class model (`v-model:filters`, an `AppliedFilter[]` distinct from the free-text `globalFilter`) mapped to the TanStack column filters client-side, or emitted for a server refetch under `manualFiltering`. A `loading` prop renders skeleton rows for dynamic (server-side) data. The root exposes a **curated imperative API** via `defineExpose` (`reload`, `clearFilters`, `exportCsv`, `getState`, `setState`) so controls or logic outside the table can drive it through a template ref, and a serializable `TableStateSnapshot` (`sorting` / `pagination` / `columnVisibility` / `columnOrder` / `globalFilter` / `filters`) is exposed via `v-model:state` + `getState()` / `setState()` + an `initialState` seed — the component stays router-agnostic, so the consuming app owns any URL / localStorage persistence. CSV serialization lives in a pure util at [`@aziontech/webkit/utils/csv`](../packages/webkit/src/utils/csv.ts) (`toCsv` + `downloadCsv`). **Types** (declared in `injection-key.ts`, re-exported for consumers): `FilterOperator` = `'eq' | 'neq' | 'contains' | 'not-contains' | 'starts-with' | 'ends-with' | 'gt' | 'gte' | 'lt' | 'lte' | 'in' | 'not-in' | 'is-empty' | 'is-not-empty'`; `FilterField` = `{ id: string; label: string; type: 'text' | 'number' | 'select' | 'multi-select' | 'boolean' | 'date'; operators?: FilterOperator[]; options?: { label: string; value: string | number | boolean }[] }`; `AppliedFilter` = `{ field: string; operator: FilterOperator; value: string | number | boolean | Array<string | number>; label?: string }`; `TableStateSnapshot` = `{ sorting?: SortingState; pagination?: PaginationState; columnVisibility?: VisibilityState; columnOrder?: string[]; globalFilter?: string; filters?: AppliedFilter[] }` (every field optional so `setState` / `initialState` accept a partial; JSON-serializable). **Collections.** `useCollection` (`@aziontech/webkit/use-collection`) drives the data-driven mode in both client and server modes: `tableProps` binds `data` (one page), `columns` (ordered by the saved preferences), `rowKey`, `loading`, `sorting`, `manualSorting` / `manualFiltering` / `manualPagination`, `paginated`, `pagination`, `rowCount`, `rowsPerPageOptions`, `enableRowSelection`, `rowSelection`, `columnVisibility` and the three display preferences (`density`, `wrapLines`, `striped`) together with their update handlers, and `exportRows`, in one `v-bind`. The table keeps rendering one page; the composable owns filtering, sorting, paging and selection across pages, so `exportRows` hands `Table.Export` and `exportCsv()` every match rather than the page: in client mode the matching items (or every item for the `all` scope), in server mode what the collection's `exportAll` callback loads (the loaded page when there is none).
useWhen: Records with the same fields shown in rows and columns, where the reader compares, sorts, selects or acts on rows (resource lists, logs, usage breakdowns).
A list needs a toolbar for search, structured filters, column visibility, CSV export or refresh — the `Table.*` toolbar parts drive the table through context.
Server-backed data that pages, sorts or filters on the API: `manual-pagination`, `manual-sorting` and `manual-filtering` emit the state instead of slicing locally.
avoidWhen: A short titled preview of a longer listing on a marketing page → use `listing-table`.
A feature-by-feature comparison of Azion with a competitor → use `comparison-table`.
Rows of mixed content (media, title, description, actions) that do not share columns → use `item`.
A grid of selectable cards or options → use `radio-cards`.
related: pagination` — the page strip; a data-driven table with `paginated` renders and wires it in the footer.
listing-table` — marketing section that composes `table` for a linked preview of a list.
empty-state` — the pattern behind the table's default `empty` slot; override the slot for resource-specific copy and actions.
item` — list rows without a column structure.
bestPractices: For repeated data, use data-driven mode: pass `data` + `columns` (any non-empty `columns` switches it on) and customize cells with the `cell-<columnId>` / `header-<columnId>` slots instead of composing N rows by hand. Compose `Table.Header` / `Table.Body` / `Table.Row` / `Table.Cell` only for small, static tables.
Give rows a stable id under `row-key` (default `'id'`); selection and `v-model:row-selection` are keyed by it.
Mark the row-actions column `kind: 'action'` so it pins to the trailing edge; give chip or short-token columns a `minWidth` rather than a fixed `width`.
Drive loading through the `loading` prop (skeleton rows, `aria-busy`) and keep the `empty` slot for no-data copy — do not swap the table for a spinner.

Place `Table.Search`, `Table.Filter`, `Table.ColumnSelector`, `Table.Export` and `Table.RefreshButton` in the `toolbar` slot with no `v-model` wiring — they read the table from context. `Table.Search` and `Table.ColumnSelector` act on the TanStack instance, so they need data-driven mode.

props.name: maxHeight
props.doc: Max height (CSS length). The viewport scrolls dynamically: horizontal scroll appears automatically when columns overflow the width; vertical scroll appears only when `maxHeight` is set smaller than the content (under the sticky header).

props.name: bordered
props.doc: Draw the outer card border around the table. Off by default (the table is typically framed by a surrounding surface); set `bordered` / `:bordered="…"` to draw the `var(--border-default)` outline. The internal row dividers are unaffected.

props.name: data
props.doc: Data-driven mode: row records.

props.name: columns
props.doc: Data-driven mode: column definitions (`{ id?, accessorKey?, header?, label?, enableSorting?, grow?, principal?, frozen?, width?, minWidth?, align?, kind?, resizable?, hideable?, orderable? }`; `width` (px) sets a fixed pixel column (also needed when a frozen column precedes another frozen column on the same edge, so sticky offsets can be summed); **`minWidth`** (px) sets a **floor** instead: the table measures the column's own content — its header, including the sort affordance, and every rendered body cell — and pins the column to the larger of the two, as **one** width applied to the header and every body cell (a per-cell `min-width` would let each row size to its own content and drift the header away from the body). It is for a column whose content is a chip or a short token: a fixed `width` there is a bet in both directions — too generous and it reserves space the rest of the row needs, too tight and the chip inside it truncates. The measured width tracks the **rendered page**, so a column can change width when paging or sorting brings longer content into view; `width` wins when both are set, and a user resize wins over both. a `grow` column without `width` keeps a shared fixed basis so the header and body stay aligned and the cell never wraps. A column with no `grow` defaults to weight `2` for the **principal** column and `1` for the rest, so the columns fill the available space proportionally. The principal column is the one flagged `principal: true`, or — when none is flagged — the first non-action column. A `kind: 'action'` column is automatically pinned to the trailing (right) edge — staying reachable while the rest scrolls horizontally — and is never resizable. **`resizable: true`** opts a column into a live mouse/touch drag-to-resize handle on its header (native pointer events; the `@tanstack/vue-table` exception covers sorting/pagination/selection/visibility, not sizing). On the first drag of any divider every flexible column freezes at its current rendered width; from then on dragging changes **only that column** and the table grows (horizontal scroll) — the others are untouched. The drag floor is the column's own content width (header label + visible body cells), so a column never shrinks past its content. Frozen and action columns ignore `resizable`. **`label`** overrides the `Table.ColumnSelector` label when `header` is not a string; **`hideable: false`** excludes the column from `Table.ColumnSelector` (e.g. the actions column); **`orderable: true`** opts the column into `columnOrder`. When non-empty, the table renders itself via TanStack.

props.name: rowKey
props.doc: Field used as the stable row id (for selection).

props.name: enableSorting
props.doc: Enable sorting globally; per-column `enableSorting` overrides.

props.name: enableRowSelection

props.name: selectOnRowClick
props.doc: Data-driven mode: clicking a row toggles its selection (requires `enableRowSelection`); interactive cells still own their own click.

props.name: headerKind
props.doc: Header density (data-driven): `compact` shrinks the column-header row's height and padding. Forwarded to the `TableHeader`'s `kind`.

props.name: paginated

props.name: pageSize
props.doc: Rows per page when paginated.

props.name: rowSelection
props.doc: v-model:rowSelection (TanStack RowSelectionState).

props.doc: v-model:columnVisibility (TanStack VisibilityState).

props.name: globalFilter

props.name: pagination
props.doc: v-model:pagination (TanStack PaginationState).

props.name: manualSorting
props.doc: Server-side sorting: emit events, do not sort locally.

props.name: manualPagination
props.doc: Server-side pagination: emit events, do not slice locally.

props.name: manualFiltering
props.doc: Server-side filtering: emit events, do not filter locally.

props.name: rowCount
props.doc: Total row count for manual pagination.

props.name: rowsPerPageOptions
props.doc: Rows-per-page options shown in the footer selector.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Data-driven mode: render skeleton rows in the body (aligned to the visible columns) and set `aria-busy`; `Table.RefreshButton` disables/spins while true. Precedence: `loading` → skeleton, else rows, else `empty`.

props.name: filters
props.doc: v-model:filters — structured applied conditions committed by `Table.Filter`, distinct from `globalFilter`. Client-side they map to TanStack column filters; under `manualFiltering` they are emitted for a server refetch.

props.name: filterFields
props.doc: Field catalog the built-in `Table.Filter` builder offers (id, label, value type, allowed operators, select options). Omit and use `Table.Filter`'s default slot to plug a custom builder.

props.name: state
props.doc: v-model:state — an aggregate serializable snapshot layered over the per-concern models. A bound per-concern v-model (e.g. `v-model:sorting`) wins over `state` for that concern.

props.name: initialState
props.doc: Uncontrolled seed applied once on mount; seeds only concerns that are not bound to their own v-model.

props.name: exportRows
props.doc: Rows `Table.Export` and `exportCsv()` write for the `filtered` and `all` scopes in place of the rows the table holds (the `page` scope always writes the rendered page). `useCollection` binds it so an export covers every match, not only the page; a promise is awaited before the `export` event and the download.

props.name: exportFilename
props.doc: Default filename for `Table.Export` and `exportCsv()` when no per-call filename is given.

props.name: stackable
props.doc: Data-driven mode: when the table's own box is narrower than `--container-lg`, each row renders as a card of label and value pairs instead of a horizontally scrolling grid. Set false to keep the grid at every width.

props.name: wrapLines
props.doc: Data-driven mode: cell text wraps onto several lines instead of truncating.

props.name: striped
props.doc: Data-driven mode: every other body row takes the raised surface.

props.name: density
props.doc: Row density: `compact` shrinks body rows and cell padding.

props.name: virtual
props.doc: Data-driven mode: render only the rows in view, for thousands of rows. The viewport scrolls vertically within `maxHeight` (40rem when empty). Ignored in the stacked layout.

props.name: estimateRowHeight
props.doc: Row height (px) assumed in `virtual` mode until a row is measured.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: Composition mode: the scrollable region (TableCaption, TableHeader, TableBody).

slots.name: footer
slots.notes: Footer region rendered below the scroll viewport (e.g. TableFooter + Pagination), so it never scrolls with the body. In data-driven mode it renders automatically when `paginated`.

slots.name: toolbar
slots.notes: Action band (search, filter trigger, refresh, export, column-selector) above the scroll viewport, end-aligned beside the title. `table` is the TanStack instance in data-driven mode, `undefined` in composition mode; `selectedRows` / `selectedCount` / `clearSelection` expose the selection for bulk-action toolbars, and `loading` mirrors the prop.

slots.name: filters
slots.notes: Active-filter chips row below the toolbar (both modes); same scope as `toolbar`.

slots.name: empty
slots.notes: Data-driven mode: shown when there are no rows. Defaults to an empty-state block (illustration + title + description) following Figma; override the slot for custom copy/actions.

table-root.purpose: Composition primitives for building accessible, pixel-perfect data tables, in two modes. **Composition mode** (default): compose the anatomy by hand (header / body / rows / cells) — the component owns markup, tokens, a11y, configurable column sizing (an emphasized first column), sortable headers, selectable rows, and a **freeze system** for sticky columns (e.g. an actions column) and a sticky header. **Data-driven mode**: pass `data` + `columns` and the table renders itself via the headless **`@tanstack/vue-table`** engine, still rendering through the same primitives (our markup/tokens/a11y, pixel-perfect to Figma). Pairs with the [`Pagination`](./pagination.md) component (rendered automatically in the footer when `paginated`). A top **toolbar band** (`title` / `toolbar` / `filters` slots) sits above the scroll viewport in both modes for a title, search / filter / export / column-selector actions, and removable filter chips; the `toolbar` and `filters` slots are scoped with the TanStack `table` instance (in data-driven mode) so the consumer can drive filtering, global search, and column visibility through the table's own methods. **Engine.** Data-driven mode is driven by **`@tanstack/vue-table`** (`useVueTable` + `getCoreRowModel` / `getSortedRowModel` / `getFilteredRowModel` / `getPaginationRowModel`), covering sorting, pagination, row selection, column visibility, and global filtering — client- and server-side (`manualSorting` / `manualPagination` / `manualFiltering`). It is a pure-logic library (no markup/styles/positioning/animation), granted narrowly to this single component per [`.claude/rules/dependencies.md`](../.claude/rules/dependencies.md) § Exceptions; rendering stays 100% in our primitives. State is exposed via v-model (`sorting`, `rowSelection`, `columnVisibility`, `globalFilter`, `pagination`, plus the structured `filters` model and the aggregate `state` snapshot below). `@tanstack/virtual` remains forbidden: the opt-in `virtual` mode windows the rows itself (spacer padding above and below the rendered slice, sized from a height index: each rendered row is measured with a `ResizeObserver`, rows not yet rendered take the average of the first rows measured, and when a row above the rows in view changes height the scroll position moves by the same amount so the rows in view stay still). Without `virtual`, a list of more than 200 rows renders its first 50 rows and mounts the rest as a spacer below them nears the viewport (an `IntersectionObserver`), so a long page costs what is on screen. **Toolbar & imperative API.** The toolbar band composes context-aware controls that drive the table through the injected context with no wiring: `Table.Filter` (a structured field/operator/value builder that commits removable/editable filter chips, with an escape slot to plug a custom builder such as the console's AQL), `Table.AppliedFilters` (the chips), `Table.ColumnSelector` (a column-visibility picker over the existing `columnVisibility` state), `Table.Export` (CSV download), and `Table.RefreshButton`. Structured filters are a first-class model (`v-model:filters`, an `AppliedFilter[]` distinct from the free-text `globalFilter`) mapped to the TanStack column filters client-side, or emitted for a server refetch under `manualFiltering`. A `loading` prop renders skeleton rows for dynamic (server-side) data. The root exposes a **curated imperative API** via `defineExpose` (`reload`, `clearFilters`, `exportCsv`, `getState`, `setState`) so controls or logic outside the table can drive it through a template ref, and a serializable `TableStateSnapshot` (`sorting` / `pagination` / `columnVisibility` / `columnOrder` / `globalFilter` / `filters`) is exposed via `v-model:state` + `getState()` / `setState()` + an `initialState` seed — the component stays router-agnostic, so the consuming app owns any URL / localStorage persistence. CSV serialization lives in a pure util at [`@aziontech/webkit/utils/csv`](../packages/webkit/src/utils/csv.ts) (`toCsv` + `downloadCsv`). **Types** (declared in `injection-key.ts`, re-exported for consumers): `FilterOperator` = `'eq' | 'neq' | 'contains' | 'not-contains' | 'starts-with' | 'ends-with' | 'gt' | 'gte' | 'lt' | 'lte' | 'in' | 'not-in' | 'is-empty' | 'is-not-empty'`; `FilterField` = `{ id: string; label: string; type: 'text' | 'number' | 'select' | 'multi-select' | 'boolean' | 'date'; operators?: FilterOperator[]; options?: { label: string; value: string | number | boolean }[] }`; `AppliedFilter` = `{ field: string; operator: FilterOperator; value: string | number | boolean | Array<string | number>; label?: string }`; `TableStateSnapshot` = `{ sorting?: SortingState; pagination?: PaginationState; columnVisibility?: VisibilityState; columnOrder?: string[]; globalFilter?: string; filters?: AppliedFilter[] }` (every field optional so `setState` / `initialState` accept a partial; JSON-serializable). **Collections.** `useCollection` (`@aziontech/webkit/use-collection`) drives the data-driven mode in both client and server modes: `tableProps` binds `data` (one page), `columns` (ordered by the saved preferences), `rowKey`, `loading`, `sorting`, `manualSorting` / `manualFiltering` / `manualPagination`, `paginated`, `pagination`, `rowCount`, `rowsPerPageOptions`, `enableRowSelection`, `rowSelection`, `columnVisibility` and the three display preferences (`density`, `wrapLines`, `striped`) together with their update handlers, and `exportRows`, in one `v-bind`. The table keeps rendering one page; the composable owns filtering, sorting, paging and selection across pages, so `exportRows` hands `Table.Export` and `exportCsv()` every match rather than the page: in client mode the matching items (or every item for the `all` scope), in server mode what the collection's `exportAll` callback loads (the loaded page when there is none).
useWhen: Records with the same fields shown in rows and columns, where the reader compares, sorts, selects or acts on rows (resource lists, logs, usage breakdowns).
A list needs a toolbar for search, structured filters, column visibility, CSV export or refresh — the `Table.*` toolbar parts drive the table through context.
Server-backed data that pages, sorts or filters on the API: `manual-pagination`, `manual-sorting` and `manual-filtering` emit the state instead of slicing locally.
avoidWhen: A short titled preview of a longer listing on a marketing page → use `listing-table`.
A feature-by-feature comparison of Azion with a competitor → use `comparison-table`.
Rows of mixed content (media, title, description, actions) that do not share columns → use `item`.
A grid of selectable cards or options → use `radio-cards`.
related: pagination` — the page strip; a data-driven table with `paginated` renders and wires it in the footer.
listing-table` — marketing section that composes `table` for a linked preview of a list.
empty-state` — the pattern behind the table's default `empty` slot; override the slot for resource-specific copy and actions.
item` — list rows without a column structure.
bestPractices: For repeated data, use data-driven mode: pass `data` + `columns` (any non-empty `columns` switches it on) and customize cells with the `cell-<columnId>` / `header-<columnId>` slots instead of composing N rows by hand. Compose `Table.Header` / `Table.Body` / `Table.Row` / `Table.Cell` only for small, static tables.
Give rows a stable id under `row-key` (default `'id'`); selection and `v-model:row-selection` are keyed by it.
Mark the row-actions column `kind: 'action'` so it pins to the trailing edge; give chip or short-token columns a `minWidth` rather than a fixed `width`.
Drive loading through the `loading` prop (skeleton rows, `aria-busy`) and keep the `empty` slot for no-data copy — do not swap the table for a spinner.

Place `Table.Search`, `Table.Filter`, `Table.ColumnSelector`, `Table.Export` and `Table.RefreshButton` in the `toolbar` slot with no `v-model` wiring — they read the table from context. `Table.Search` and `Table.ColumnSelector` act on the TanStack instance, so they need data-driven mode.

props.name: query
props.doc: The tokens and how they combine. Supports v-model:query.

props.name: properties
props.doc: Properties the suggestions offer, with their operators and values.

props.name: totalCount
props.doc: Items that match the query, announced next to the tokens. Hidden when unset.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Placeholder of the field. Empty uses the locale catalog.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the field. Empty uses the locale catalog.

props.name: freeText
props.doc: Accepts typed text with no property as a free-text token.

events.notes: A token was added or removed, the operation changed, or all cleared.

property-filter.purpose: One field that filters a collection by properties and free text, after Cloudscape's property filter. Typing suggests a property, then an operator, then a value, and each choice becomes a removable token (`Status = Active`); text typed without a property becomes a free-text token. Two or more tokens combine with Match all (and) or Match any (or). It edits a `PropertyFilterQuery` and never filters anything itself: `useCollection` (or the server) applies the query, and `propertyFilterProps` binds the query, the properties and the match count in one `v-bind`.
useWhen: A list or table that people narrow by several fields at once (status, region, owner) and by text.
Any collection driven by `useCollection`, client or server mode.
Filters that must survive a reload or a shared link: the query serializes into the URL through `useCollection`.
avoidWhen: A single text search over a short list → use `input` bound to `filterProps`.
A few fixed choices always on screen → use `toggle-group` or `chip` filters.
A structured filter builder with its own panel inside a table toolbar → use `table-filter`.
related: use-collection` — applies the query; `propertyFilterProps` is the binding.
table` — the collection it usually filters.
cards` — the card form of a collection.
collection-preferences` — the panel that sits beside it in the controls row.
bestPractices: Give every property with a closed set of values its `options`, so values are suggested and tokens print labels.
Set `type: 'number'` or `type: 'date'` on ordered properties to offer `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`.
Bind `totalCount` so people hear how many items match after each change.
Name the field after the collection (`aria-label="Filter resources"`).

props.name: preferences
props.doc: The saved preferences. Supports v-model:preferences; changes apply on Confirm.

props.name: columns
props.doc: Columns to show, hide and order. Empty hides the columns section.

props.name: pageSizeOptions

props.name: sections

props.name: container
props.doc: Opens in a centered dialog or a side drawer.

props.name: title

props.name: disabled

events.name: update:preferences

events.name: confirm

events.name: cancel

slots.name: trigger

collection-preferences.purpose: The preferences panel of a collection, after Cloudscape's collection preferences: a cog button opens a dialog (or a drawer) with the page size, the columns (shown, hidden and ordered; a locked column always shows), wrapped lines, striped rows and density. Changes are a draft until Confirm; Cancel, `Esc` and the close button discard them. It holds no saved state itself: `useCollection` saves the confirmed value in `localStorage` and `preferencesProps` binds the value, the columns and the page sizes in one `v-bind`.
useWhen: A table or card collection whose people choose how many items a page shows and which fields they see.
Any collection driven by `useCollection`, which saves the result per collection.
avoidWhen: A single column-visibility toggle inside a table toolbar → use `table-column-selector`.
Settings of the resource itself (not of how the list shows it) → use a form page or `dialog`.
related: use-collection` — saves the preferences; `preferencesProps` is the binding.
table` — takes `density`, `wrapLines`, `striped`, the visible columns and their order.
cards` — takes the page size and the visible fields.
property-filter` — sits beside it in the controls row.
bestPractices: Lock the column that names the item (`locked: true`): a row without its name is unreadable.
Show only the sections the collection uses (`sections`): cards have no striped rows.
Keep the trigger at the end of the controls row, after Refresh and Download.

props.name: loading

props.name: ariaLabel

slots.scope: { item: Record<string, unknown>; index: number; selected: boolean }
slots.notes: Card title; names the card and its selection control.

slots.name: default

slots.notes: Card body: the item's fields.

slots.name: empty

cards.purpose: A collection shown as cards, after Cloudscape's cards: one card per item, named by its `header` slot, with the item's fields in the default slot. It shares Table's item and selection model — `items`, `trackBy`, `selectedKeys` — so `useCollection` binds it through `cardsProps`, and selection (single or multi, with a visible select-all) survives paging. Four cards a row in a wide container, then three, two and one as the container narrows.
useWhen: Items people recognise by a few fields or a picture rather than compare column by column (applications, templates, environments).
The card form of a list page (`platform/view/card-view`), filtered and paged by `useCollection`.
avoidWhen: Records compared, sorted or scanned across many fields → use `table`.
A fixed marketing grid of features or links → use `card-grid`.
A single content box → use `card`.
related: use-collection` — filters, pages and selects; `cardsProps` is the binding.
table` — the same collection as rows; same item and selection model.
property-filter`, `collection-preferences`, `pagination` — the controls around it.
card` — one standalone card.
bestPractices: Put the item's name, as a link to the item, in the `header` slot: it also names the selection control.
Keep each card to a handful of label and value pairs; let `collection-preferences` choose which.
Use `selectionMode="multi"` only when a bulk action exists next to the list.

slots.name: default

pagination.purpose: Pagination controls for tables and lists, pixel-perfect to Figma, in two modes. **Composition mode** (default): a three-region landmark — page-info text, navigation buttons (Previous / page numbers / overflow / Next), and a rows-per-page selector — wired by hand through slots, with the consumer owning the current page, total, and page-size state. **Data-driven mode**: pass `total` (and optionally `page` / `pageSize`) and the Pagination renders its own info text, Previous / windowed page numbers / overflow ellipsis / Next, and the rows-per-page selector, emitting `update:page` / `update:pageSize` so the consumer can bind state via `v-model`. This component owns markup, tokens, and a11y; the data engine is a small internal page-window calculation — **no external pagination library**. Pairs with the [`Table`](./table.md) component.
useWhen: A list or table outside `table`'s own footer needs page navigation and a rows-per-page selector.
You know the item count — pass `total` and bind `v-model:page` / `v-model:page-size`; the component renders the info text, the windowed page numbers and the selector.
The page strip needs custom content (a different info line, extra controls) — compose `Pagination.Info`, `Pagination.Button` and `Pagination.PageSize` through the slots.
avoidWhen: The rows live in a data-driven `table` → set `paginated` on the table; it renders this pagination in its footer and wires it for you.
It is the previous / next pair at the end of a documentation page → use `doc-pagination`.
The content loads more as the reader scrolls or clicks "Load more" → use a `button` at the end of the list.
related: table` — renders a wired pagination in its footer when `paginated` is set.
doc-pagination` — previous / next links between documentation pages, not numbered pages of a list.
bestPractices: Prefer data-driven mode (`total` set); in composition mode the root emits nothing and you own every button's `selected` / `disabled` state and every click.
page` is 1-based. Changing the page size through the selector emits `update:pageSize` and resets the page to `1`.
Keep `page-size-options` aligned with what your data source accepts; the default is `[10, 25, 50, 100]`.
Tune `sibling-count` (default `1`) instead of hiding buttons — it controls how many numbers sit on each side of the current page before the overflow ellipsis.
Set `aria-label` when a page carries more than one pagination, so each navigation landmark has a distinct name.

props.doc: Total item count. When set, the Pagination runs in data-driven mode and renders its own controls.

props.doc: Rows per page (data-driven mode). Supports `v-model:page-size`.

props.doc: Accessible name for the navigation landmark. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Pagination`).

events.name: update:page
events.notes: Current page changed in data-driven mode (Previous / Next / page number). Supports `v-model:page`.

events.name: update:pageSize
events.notes: Rows-per-page changed via the internal selector. Supports `v-model:page-size`.

slots.name: info
slots.notes: Left region: page-info text (typically PaginatorInfo). In data-driven mode, overrides the default "Showing X to Y of Z entries" text.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: Center region: pagination navigation buttons (composition mode only — ignored in data-driven mode, where the buttons are rendered internally).

slots.name: controls
slots.notes: Right region: rows-per-page selector (PaginatorPageSize). In data-driven mode, overrides the internally-rendered selector.

pagination-root.purpose: Pagination controls for tables and lists, pixel-perfect to Figma, in two modes. **Composition mode** (default): a three-region landmark — page-info text, navigation buttons (Previous / page numbers / overflow / Next), and a rows-per-page selector — wired by hand through slots, with the consumer owning the current page, total, and page-size state. **Data-driven mode**: pass `total` (and optionally `page` / `pageSize`) and the Pagination renders its own info text, Previous / windowed page numbers / overflow ellipsis / Next, and the rows-per-page selector, emitting `update:page` / `update:pageSize` so the consumer can bind state via `v-model`. This component owns markup, tokens, and a11y; the data engine is a small internal page-window calculation — **no external pagination library**. Pairs with the [`Table`](./table.md) component.
useWhen: A list or table outside `table`'s own footer needs page navigation and a rows-per-page selector.
You know the item count — pass `total` and bind `v-model:page` / `v-model:page-size`; the component renders the info text, the windowed page numbers and the selector.
The page strip needs custom content (a different info line, extra controls) — compose `Pagination.Info`, `Pagination.Button` and `Pagination.PageSize` through the slots.
avoidWhen: The rows live in a data-driven `table` → set `paginated` on the table; it renders this pagination in its footer and wires it for you.
It is the previous / next pair at the end of a documentation page → use `doc-pagination`.
The content loads more as the reader scrolls or clicks "Load more" → use a `button` at the end of the list.
related: table` — renders a wired pagination in its footer when `paginated` is set.
doc-pagination` — previous / next links between documentation pages, not numbered pages of a list.
bestPractices: Prefer data-driven mode (`total` set); in composition mode the root emits nothing and you own every button's `selected` / `disabled` state and every click.
page` is 1-based. Changing the page size through the selector emits `update:pageSize` and resets the page to `1`.
Keep `page-size-options` aligned with what your data source accepts; the default is `[10, 25, 50, 100]`.
Tune `sibling-count` (default `1`) instead of hiding buttons — it controls how many numbers sit on each side of the current page before the overflow ellipsis.
Set `aria-label` when a page carries more than one pagination, so each navigation landmark has a distinct name.

props.name: kind
props.doc: Button role within the pagination.

props.name: selected
props.doc: Marks the current page (filled surface + aria-current).

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens.

events.name: click
events.notes: Fires on activation. Not emitted while `disabled` (the native `disabled` attribute also blocks it), and never for `kind="more"`.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The page number. Rendered only when `kind` is `number`.

pagination-button.purpose: PaginationButton is one segment of the pagination's numbers strip: a 28px-tall native `button` that renders a page number or a Previous / Next chevron, or — for `kind="more"` — an inert, decorative overflow ellipsis (`span`, `aria-hidden`), selected by `kind`. It is the part `pagination` renders in data-driven mode and the one consumers compose by hand in composition mode, where it is reached as `Pagination.Button` (or imported standalone from `@aziontech/webkit/pagination-button`). It owns the segment's surface, current-page (`selected`) and `disabled` treatment, but not the strip's frame, border or the page state, which belong to the `pagination` root and the consumer.
useWhen: Compose a custom page strip inside `pagination`'s default slot (composition mode), one button per Previous, page number, overflow and Next.
Render the current page of a hand-wired pagination with `selected`, and the unavailable Previous / Next ends with `disabled`.
avoidWhen: You know the item count → pass `total` to `pagination` and bind `v-model:page`; it renders and wires every PaginationButton itself.
The rows live in a data-driven `table` → set `paginated` on the table instead.
The control is a previous / next link between documentation pages → use `doc-pagination`.
It is a standalone action outside a pagination strip → use `button` or `icon-button`; this button has no radius or frame of its own except at the strip's ends.
It is a "Load more" control at the end of a list → use `button`.
related: pagination` — the root that frames the strip and, in data-driven mode, renders these buttons; re-exports this component as `Pagination.Button`.
pagination-info` — the page-info text that sits beside the strip.
pagination-page-size` — the rows-per-page selector placed in the pagination's `controls` slot.
icon-button` — a standalone icon-only action with its own frame and radius.
bestPractices: Place it only inside `pagination`'s default slot: the strip's border and frame come from the root, and the outer radius is applied through `first:` / `last:`, so only the first and last buttons of the strip round their corners.

Pass `aria-label` on every `previous` and `next` button: those kinds render an `aria-hidden` icon only and have no accessible name otherwise. `more` is decorative and hidden from assistive tech, so it takes no `aria-label`.
Put the page number in the default slot of `kind="number"` only; the other kinds ignore the slot.
Set `selected` on exactly one number button (it sets `aria-current="page"`), and `disabled` on Previous at the first page and Next at the last.
In composition mode you own every click: listen to `click` and update the page yourself; a `disabled` button never emits it.

props.name: align
props.doc: Vertical alignment of nodes within the diagram.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: Diagram content: `flow-node` and `flow-parallel`, in flow order.

flow.purpose: Flow renders a directed flow diagram: a horizontal sequence of steps (`flow-node`) joined by decorative connectors, with optional parallel branches (`flow-parallel`) and custom connector-attachment points (`flow-anchor`). Use it to visualize pipelines, workflows, and step-by-step processes inside a data view; unlike `table` it expresses ordered/branching relationships rather than tabular records. Steps are written as direct children of `flow`; a `flow-parallel` between two steps fans out from the previous step and fans back into the next, and a `flow-parallel` at the start/end fans only inward/outward (no dangling stubs). A node can be styled (the default box) or `unstyled` so its slot content defines the entire node — a dot, a tall card, a multi-row card — while connectors still attach correctly, optionally at `flow-anchor` points inside the node. Connectors run port-to-port: a styled node renders a small square **connector port** just outside each of its edges, and a `flow-anchor` renders one outside the edge it attaches to, so a line always terminates on a visible attachment point instead of a bare edge (the port is the endpoint treatment — connectors carry no arrowheads). The port sits fully clear of the box rather than overlapping it, so neither the node's surface nor its focus ring crops it. A port is only rendered where a connector actually attaches: the leading child has no incoming connector and the trailing child no outgoing one, so those two edges show no port and the chain opens and closes on a node rather than on a stub. An `unstyled` node renders no ports, because its slot content owns its appearance; put a `flow-anchor` inside it to place ports on the parts a connector should touch. Design source (rewritten to our conventions, never inherited as-is): the kumo "Flow" component group at https://kumo-ui.com/components/flow/. Scope boundary: large diagrams pan via a native `overflow: auto` scroll container on the root — free 2D drag-pan is intentionally out of scope (it would require an external positioning library forbidden by `.claude/rules/dependencies.md`). The connector port is specified by the Figma frame in the frontmatter; the remaining tokens are inferred from intent and recorded in the Theme gaps table.
useWhen: Showing an ordered pipeline or request path as steps joined by connectors — build → deploy → serve, or a request through a load balancer, a function and its bindings.
A step fans out to several parallel targets and (optionally) back in — wrap those steps in `Flow.Parallel`.
A node with custom content (a card with several rows) where connectors must touch specific parts — mark them with `Flow.Anchor`.
avoidWhen: One of the official architecture drawings, or a node-and-connector picture for a marketing page → use `diagram`.
Tabular records with no ordering between them → use `table`.
A numbered set of instructions in documentation → use `doc-steps`.
related: diagram` — marketing architecture drawings from a closed library or a one-off spec; `flow` is the in-product, hand-composed pipeline.
doc-steps` — an ordered walkthrough of text steps joined by a rail, not connected nodes.
table` — records without ordered or branching relationships.
bestPractices: Write steps as direct children of `Flow` in flow order; connectors are drawn between siblings, so wrapping nodes in extra elements breaks the chain.

Use `unstyled` when the slot content is the whole node, and put a `Flow.Anchor` (`type="end"` incoming, `type="start"` outgoing) on each part a connector should touch — an unstyled node renders no ports of its own.
Mark a leaf that hangs off the chain with `terminal`; it receives a connector but sends none on.
Do not clip a node with `overflow-hidden` in a wrapping card — the connector ports sit outside the node's box and would disappear.
Let a wide flow scroll in its own container; the root is an `overflow: auto` region, and there is no drag-to-pan.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: Bound pair of lists as `[sourceItems, targetItems]` (v-model).

props.name: dataKey
props.doc: Item field used as each row's render key (falls back to the index). Selection is always tracked by index.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables all selection and move controls and applies disabled tokens.

props.name: moveOnDoubleClick
props.doc: When true, double-clicking an item moves it to the opposite list. Set false to keep `item-double-click` firing without the move.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.notes: v-model update with the new `[sourceItems, targetItems]` pair.

events.name: move
events.notes: Fired after items move between lists, with the moved items.

events.name: item-double-click
events.payload: (event: MouseEvent, payload: { list: 'source' | 'target'; item: unknown; index: number })
events.notes: Fired when an option is double-clicked. `event` is the dblclick; `payload` carries the item, its index, and which list it was in. Fires regardless of `moveOnDoubleClick`, but not while the component is disabled or a list is loading.

slots.name: default
slots.scope: { move, moveAll, hasSelection, count, disabled, loading }
slots.notes: Composition slot; receives `<PickList.Source>`, `<PickList.Controls>`, and `<PickList.Target>` in flow order. The scope exposes the move actions plus selection/loading state, so a consumer can render custom controls inside the root in place of `<PickList.Controls>`.

pick-list.purpose: Dual-list transfer control: a labelled **source** listbox and a labelled **target** listbox with a control column to move items between them. Use it when the consumer needs to build a subset from a pool of options where both the chosen set and the remaining pool stay visible. Derived from the PrimeVue PickList behavior but rewritten to our conventions (no Figma); the visual surface is a best-effort first draft to validate. Compound, composition API: the root (`<PickList>`) owns the bound data (`v-model` = `[sourceItems, targetItems]`) and the shared selection/move state, and provides it through `provide`/`inject`. The consumer composes the anatomy — `<PickList.Source>`, `<PickList.Controls>`, `<PickList.Target>` — and the context-aware `<PickList.Controls>` wires the move buttons with no props. Each list is data-driven: items come from the root's bound pair and render through the list's `#item` slot (repeated data stays as props, not hand-authored rows). Double-clicking an option moves it to the opposite list (emitting `item-double-click`); this auto-move can be turned off with `move-on-double-click`. The two lists sit side by side on wider viewports and stack vertically (with the controls as a horizontal row between them) on narrow ones; the move arrows point left/right side-by-side and up/down when stacked.
useWhen: Building a subset from a pool where both the chosen and the remaining items stay visible (domains assigned to an application, members of a team).
Moving many items at once with move-all and multi-selection.
Lists that load separately, each with its own `loading` state.
avoidWhen: Picking a few values in a compact field → use `multi-select`.
Selecting rows of tabular data with columns, sorting, or pagination → use `table` with row selection.
A handful of fixed options → use a horizontal `field` with a `checkbox` for each.
related: multi-select` — compact dropdown for multi-pick when the remaining pool does not need to stay visible.
table` — row selection over tabular data.
checkbox` — independent boolean or small-set multi-pick.
bestPractices: Set `data-key` to a unique item field so rows keep stable keys across moves; without it rows are keyed by their index.
Set `title` on both `PickList.Source` and `PickList.Target`; it is the listbox's accessible name.
Listen to `move` for side effects such as saving the assignment instead of diffing `v-model`.
Set `:move-on-double-click="false"` when double-click should do something else; `item-double-click` still fires.
