Each card keeps its title with a Hint and nothing else in its header, and shows a Tag with its span while editing. The page owns the layout, an array of id, span and height bound with v-model:span and v-model:height, and the order, which it changes on drop or on the arrow keys of a focused drag handle, then puts focus back on the moved handle and announces the move in a polite live region. Reset layout appears once the layout differs from the default. Keep the layout wherever the product stores preferences. Built from `PageHeader`, `ChartCard` (with its drag handle and resize corner), `Chart`, `DonutChart`, `BarList`, `Hint`, `Tag` and `Button`.
platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboar.guidelinesSummary: A dashboard the reader arranges: they move cards, change how many columns a card spans and how tall it is, and keep that layout. It serves readers who come back to the same page every day and care about different cards than the default puts first. The page owns the layout (an array of id, span and height) and the order; `ChartCard` provides the drag handle, the resize corner and their keyboard model.

variants.name: Editing
variants.summary: Edit mode. Drag a card by its handle onto another to swap their order, or drag its corner to change the span and the height. Focus the handle and use the arrow keys to move a card, or focus the corner and use Left and Right for the span, Up and Down for the height.

variants.name: Loading
variants.summary: While the data loads, every chart renders its own Skeleton inside its card, so the layout holds its shape.

variants.name: Empty
variants.summary: Nothing recorded yet. Each card keeps its place and size and shows its empty state, so the reader can still arrange the dashboard before any data arrives.

variants.name: Failed
variants.summary: The request for the cards failed: every card keeps its place, size and header, with a danger Alert that names the card that did not load and offers Retry.

platform/dashboard/data-dashboard.name: DataDashboard
platform/dashboard/data-dashboard.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/DataDashboard
platform/dashboard/data-dashboard.summary: The data dashboard pattern: KPI tiles with sparklines and period-over-period deltas, followed by the breakdowns that explain them. Six StatTiles carry each metric’s period total, a sparkline and the change against the previous 24 hours, each with a Hint that defines the metric. Under them, a ChartCard draws data transferred this period over the previous one as two series, a labeled horizontal bar Chart ranks the projects by data transferred, and a searchable, paginated TableRoot lists requests and data transferred per project. Every card keeps its Sum and change Tags, an Expand IconButton and a DropdownMenu with Copy query and Export CSV. Built from `PageHeader`, `StatTile`, `ChartCard`, `Chart`, `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `Hint`, `ToggleGroup`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `DropdownMenu`, `Input` and `EmptyState`.
platform/dashboard/data-dashboard.guidelinesSummary: The usage page: how much the account's projects consumed in the period, how that compares with the previous period, and which projects drove it. It leads with six KPI tiles (each with a sparkline and the change against the previous 24 hours), then explains the headline number with this period against the previous one, a ranking of projects and a table of usage per project.

variants.name: Loading
variants.summary: The first response is on its way: Skeletons hold every tile, chart and table row in place.

variants.name: Empty
variants.summary: No usage recorded yet: each tile shows a dash, and every chart and the table explain that nothing was recorded in the period.

variants.name: Failed
variants.summary: The request for the period failed: the tiles read as dashes, and every card keeps its header with a danger Alert that names what did not load and offers Retry.

platform/dashboard/executive-summary-das.name: ExecutiveSummaryDashboard
platform/dashboard/executive-summary-das.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/ExecutiveSummaryDashboard
platform/dashboard/executive-summary-das.summary: An executive summary dashboard: one page a lead reads to see how the quarter went. A page heading with the quarter Select and Export sits over a scorecard row of six StatTiles (revenue, monthly active users, net revenue retention, NPS, uptime and cost per request), each with its delta against last quarter and a Hint that defines it. Below, a trend grid of small multiples, one ChartCard per metric with a compact Chart (Area or Line) over the last 12 months and a Tag with the twelve-month change, shares one active index so hovering a month moves the crosshair on every card. A side column holds the goals, a Card of goal bars where each goal shows its label, a status Tag (On track, At risk, Off track), a Progress of current against target and both figures, and the commentary, a Card of Item rows with the author Avatar, role, date and the note itself. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`.
platform/dashboard/executive-summary-das.guidelinesSummary: The one page a lead reads to see how the quarter went: the headline results against last quarter, the twelve-month trend behind each one, progress on the quarter's goals and the notes the leads wrote when they reviewed it. It favours a few numbers read in seconds over detail; every figure links back to its own dashboard for the breakdown.

variants.name: Loading
variants.summary: While the quarter loads, the tiles and charts render their own Skeleton and the goals and commentary hold Skeleton rows, so the page does not reflow when data arrives.

variants.name: Empty
variants.summary: A quarter with nothing reported. The tiles show a dash with no delta, every trend card keeps its box with an EmptyState that names the quarter and points to a later one, and the goals and commentary each say what fills them.

variants.name: Failed
variants.summary: The request for the quarter failed: the tiles read as dashes, and every trend card, the goals and the commentary keep their header with a danger Alert that names what did not load and offers Retry.

platform/dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboa.name: FunnelCohortDashboard
platform/dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboa.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/FunnelCohortDashboard
platform/dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboa.summary: A funnel and cohort dashboard: how people move through the steps from a first visit to a paid plan, and how well each weekly sign-up cohort is retained. The page opens with a heading and one global filter bar, a period and a segment `Select`, so every region renders the same slice. Below it, a row of five `StatTile`s (visitors, sign-ups, activated, paid and overall conversion, each against the previous period with a sparkline) sits over a 12-column grid of `ChartCard`s. The conversion funnel spans the grid: a horizontal, labeled `Chart.Bar` of the steps beside a `TableRoot` that states each step’s users, its share of visitors and the drop-off from the step before. Cohort retention shares the next row: a multi-series `Chart.Line` of retention by week since sign-up, one series per weekly cohort, and a cohort `TableRoot` with each cohort’s size and its week 1 to week 6 retention in tabular figures, where a dash marks a week that has not ended. There is no heatmap: the retention matrix is a plain table, not colored cells. Each card header carries a title with a `Hint` and a menu with Export CSV. Built from `PageHeader`, `Select`, `StatTile`, `ChartCard`, `Chart`, `TableRoot`, `EmptyState`, `Hint`, `DropdownMenu`, `IconButton` and `Button`.
platform/dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboa.guidelinesSummary: The growth page: how people move through the steps from a first visit to a paid plan, where they drop off, and how well each weekly sign-up cohort keeps coming back. One global filter bar (period and segment) drives every region, so the funnel, the tiles and the cohorts always describe the same slice of users.

variants.name: Loading
variants.summary: While the first response loads, every tile, both charts and both tables hold their place with a Skeleton, so the grid does not reflow when data arrives. The filter bar stays usable.

variants.name: Empty
variants.summary: The filters match nothing. The tiles show a dash with no delta or trend, and each card keeps its box with an EmptyState that names the filters as the reason and offers Clear filters, which resets the period and the segment.

variants.name: Failed
variants.summary: The request for the period failed: the tiles read as dashes, and every card keeps its header with a danger Alert that names what did not load and offers Retry.

platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboar.name: HealthScoreDashboard
platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboar.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/HealthScoreDashboard
platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboar.summary: A health score dashboard: how well something performs for the people who use it, read as one score out of 100 and its bands. A page heading with the period Select sits over the overall score, a ChartCard with the figure, its band Tag (Good at 80 or more, Fair from 50 to 79, Poor under 50), the top cause of poor samples and a Line Chart of the score per hour. Two ChartCards rank the score per application and per location in a BarList, lowest first, each row naming its top cause. An hourly score card gives every application a Tracker strip, one block per hour colored by band, with its current band Tag at the end of the row. Under the grid, a Card lists the open incidents as Item rows: what is affected, the cause, how many devices and what share of samples, when it opened, and its band. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`.
platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboar.guidelinesSummary: The page that answers "how well does this work for the people who use it, and where is it worst?". Experience is reduced to one score out of 100 with three bands (Good at 80 or more, Fair from 50 to 79, Poor under 50). The page shows the overall score and its trend, ranks applications and locations lowest first with the top cause of poor samples, gives each application an hour-by-hour strip, and ends in the open incidents that need someone's attention.

variants.name: Loading
variants.summary: While the period loads, the chart, the rankings and the trackers render their own Skeleton and the incidents hold Skeleton rows, so the page does not reflow when data arrives.

variants.name: Empty
variants.summary: A period with no samples. The score shows a dash with no band, and every region keeps its box with an empty state that names the period and says what fills it.

variants.name: Failed
variants.summary: The request for the period failed: the score shows a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger Alert that names what did not load and offers Retry.

platform/dashboard/home-dashboard.name: HomeDashboard
platform/dashboard/home-dashboard.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/HomeDashboard
platform/dashboard/home-dashboard.summary: The whole Home page inside the platform shell, in both of its states. **Populated** (once the account owns a resource): a greeting heading, a usage band with four chartless StatTiles (each label explained in a Tooltip in the tile’s aside slot, each figure beside its unit and delta Tag) next to the dismissible agent onboarding card, and a five-column resources grid with the Projects, Resources, Domains and Recents panels, every row a full-width link with a hover-revealed actions DropdownMenu. **Empty** (a brand-new account): the first-access screen, a greeting under a centred headline, the command prompt that opens the shell’s palette on click or Enter, and the three doors (ship something new, add a domain with its availability check, onboard your agent). The first-access content on its own is the Onboarding template; while either screen arrives, the PageWires Overview and Onboarding wires hold the page. Built from `StatTile`, `Card`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `Item`, `DropdownMenu`, `Input`, `Kbd`, `Popover`, `Spinner`, `Illustration`, `Button` and the agent marks from the webkit assets.
platform/dashboard/home-dashboard.guidelinesSummary: The Console's Home page inside the platform shell: the first screen a signed-in user lands on. Its job is to get them back to work fast. For an account that owns resources it shows a short usage band and the resources they touch most (projects, resources, domains, recents), every row a link. For a brand-new account it becomes the first-access screen: a greeting, the command prompt and three doors to a first project, a first domain and a coding agent. It is not an analytics page; detail lives on each resource's own dashboard.

variants.name: Empty
variants.summary: Home for a brand-new account: the first-access screen in the shell. Click the prompt (or press Enter on it) to open the command palette; type a domain such as example.com (taken) or my-new-site.dev (available) into the second door to run the availability check.

platform/dashboard/project-status-dashbo.name: ProjectStatusDashboard
platform/dashboard/project-status-dashbo.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/ProjectStatusDashboard
platform/dashboard/project-status-dashbo.summary: A project status dashboard: where a project stands against its plan, for one project and sprint at a time. The page opens with a PageHeader whose actions hold two Selects (project and sprint), then a row of four StatTiles (completion, tasks done, open tasks and overdue, each against the previous sprint), over a 12-column grid of ChartCards. A DonutChart splits every task by status (done, in progress, not started, and blocked in the danger color) beside the sprint burndown, a Chart of two Lines (actual story points left against the ideal straight line to zero) tagged with how far behind the sprint runs. The milestone timeline and the at-risk list share the next row: the timeline is an Item list with the date, title and a StatusIndicator per checkpoint, since there is no timeline component; the at-risk list is Item rows with the reason and a Tag. The owners table closes the grid, a TableRoot with each owner’s Avatar and name, open and done counts, and overdue as a danger Tag. Every card carries the same header: title with a Hint, its tags, and a menu with Copy link and Export CSV. Built from `PageHeader`, `StatTile`, `ChartCard`, `DonutChart`, `Chart`, `Item`, `StatusIndicator`, `TableRoot`, `Avatar`, `Tag`, `Select`, `Hint`, `DropdownMenu`, `EmptyState`, `Skeleton` and `Button`.
platform/dashboard/project-status-dashbo.guidelinesSummary: Where one project stands against its plan, one project and sprint at a time. A lead or a team member opens it before a stand-up or a review to see completion, the sprint burndown, the next milestones, what is at risk and who carries the open work. The page heading (`Project status`) sits over a filter row that picks the project and the sprint; every region reads that pair.

variants.name: Loading
variants.summary: While the first response loads, the tiles, both charts and the table hold their place with a Skeleton, and the two lists show Skeleton rows, so the grid does not reflow when data arrives.

variants.name: Empty
variants.summary: A project with no tasks yet. The tiles show a dash with no delta or trend, every card keeps its box with an EmptyState that says what will appear there, and the completion card carries the one setup action, Add tasks.

variants.name: Failed
variants.summary: The request for the period failed: the tiles read as dashes, and every card keeps its header with a danger Alert that names what did not load and offers Retry.

platform/dashboard/scan-results-dashboar.name: ScanResultsDashboard
platform/dashboard/scan-results-dashboar.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/ScanResultsDashboard
platform/dashboard/scan-results-dashboar.summary: A scan results dashboard: items sent for analysis, the verdict each one received and what is still waiting. A page heading with a Refresh IconButton sits over a row of six StatTiles (submitted, in analysis, last 24 hours, flagged, held for a verdict and open alerts), each with a Hint that defines it. Below, three cards share a row: a DonutChart of the verdicts (Clean, Suspicious, Flagged and Pending, in their status hues) with the item count in its center, a BarList of the sources the items came from, and a Card that sums up the deliveries held for a verdict and the items delivered before they were flagged, each with a Link to its list. A Submissions card across the full width holds the filter row (an Input search and Selects for status, verdict and source) over a paginated TableRoot: name, the verdict Tag, category, score, type, size, source, first submitter and last seen. Built from `PageHeader`, `StatTile`, `DonutChart`, `BarList`, `ChartCard`, `Card`, `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `Link`, `Input`, `Select`, `Hint`, `IconButton`, `Skeleton` and `EmptyState`.
platform/dashboard/scan-results-dashboar.guidelinesSummary: The page for a pipeline that sends items (files, attachments, packages) for analysis and gives each a verdict. The reader checks what was submitted, what is still waiting, what was flagged, and above all two exceptions: deliveries held until a verdict arrives, and items that were delivered before they were flagged. It ends in the submissions table, where the reader finds a specific item.

variants.name: Loading
variants.summary: While the results load, the tiles, the donut and the bar list render their own Skeleton, the summary holds Skeleton lines and the table shows Skeleton rows, so the page does not reflow when data arrives.

variants.name: Empty
variants.summary: Nothing has been sent for analysis yet. The tiles read zero, the verdicts and sources keep their box with an EmptyState, and the Submissions card drops the filters and the table for one EmptyState that says what fills it.

variants.name: Failed
variants.summary: The request for the period failed: the tiles read as dashes, and every card keeps its header with a danger Alert that names what did not load and offers Retry.

platform/dashboard/security-dashboard.name: SecurityDashboard
platform/dashboard/security-dashboard.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/SecurityDashboard
platform/dashboard/security-dashboard.summary: The security dashboard pattern: blocked and allowed requests over time, breakdowns by attack category and origin, the top sources and an attention list. A row of three StatTiles (Requests blocked, Requests inspected, Block rate, each with its delta against the previous period and a sparkline) sits over a 12-column grid of ChartCards. Matched requests over time plots blocked and logged requests; Needs attention lists the settings and traffic that ask for a decision, each with a severity Tag and one action Link; attack categories and countries read as ranked BarLists, and the top source IPs as a searchable, paginated TableRoot. With no rule set in place the tiles stay as dashes and one setup EmptyState that offers Add rule set replaces the grid. Built from `PageHeader`, `StatTile`, `ChartCard`, `Chart`, `BarList`, `Item`, `Tag`, `Link`, `TableRoot`, `Hint`, `ToggleGroup`, `DropdownMenu`, `Skeleton`, `EmptyState` and `Button`.
platform/dashboard/security-dashboard.guidelinesSummary: The page a reader opens to see what their security rules are doing: how many requests were blocked and inspected, how blocking moved over time, which attack categories and countries it came from, which source addresses sent the most, and the short list of settings and traffic that need a decision now. Needs attention is what makes it more than a report: every entry ends in one action.

variants.name: Loading
variants.summary: The first load: every tile, chart and the table hold a Skeleton, and Needs attention shows three placeholder rows.

variants.name: Empty
variants.summary: No security rules set up yet: the tiles read as dashes, and one bordered EmptyState names the reason and offers Add rule set instead of a grid of empty charts.

variants.name: Failed
variants.summary: The request for the period failed: the tiles read as dashes, and every card keeps its header with a danger Alert that names what did not load and offers Retry.

platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-da.name: ServiceMonitoringDashboard
platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-da.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/ServiceMonitoringDashboard
platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-da.summary: The service monitoring dashboard pattern: status tiles with sparklines, multi-series charts and an alert rail. One StatTile per service carries its p95 latency, the change against the previous period and a sparkline, with a StatusIndicator naming its state in words. Below, Latency (p50, p95, p99) and Error rate (Status 4xx, Status 5xx) sit in ChartCards as multi-series line Charts, each with its own window ToggleGroup, while an Open alerts rail holds the right edge: a fixed-width column that scrolls on its own, independent of the tiles and charts, listing each alert as an Item in an Item.Group with a severity Tag. Under the xl breakpoint the rail folds below the charts and the page scrolls as one. Built from `StatTile`, `StatusIndicator`, `ChartCard`, `Chart`, `ToggleGroup`, `Hint`, `Item`, `Tag`, `Skeleton` and `EmptyState`.
platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-da.guidelinesSummary: The page an on-call engineer keeps open: is every service up, how fast is it answering, how many requests fail, and which alerts are open right now. One tile per service states its p95 latency and its state in words; latency percentiles and error rates sit in two charts with their own window; the open alerts live in a rail on the right that scrolls on its own, so the alerts stay in view while the reader studies a chart.

variants.name: Loading
variants.summary: The first load: every tile, both charts and the rail hold Skeletons, and the window switches stay usable.

variants.name: Empty
variants.summary: No traffic yet: the tiles show a dash, both charts explain that metrics appear once a service serves requests, and the rail reads No open alerts.

variants.name: Failed
variants.summary: The request for the window failed: each service tile reads as a dash, and both charts and the Open alerts rail show a danger Alert that names what did not load and offers Retry.

platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation.name: DeleteWithConfirmation
platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation.title: Templates/Platform/Delete/DeleteWithConfirmation
platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation.summary: The destructive confirmation a resource list uses for Delete: a warning `Alert`, a sentence naming what goes with the resource and a Help Center link, then a prompt that shows the resource name as a click-to-copy chip and an input the user must match before Delete enables. Every resource list, a folder of files and a table of records open it from the row Delete action; the title reads Delete plus the resource kind, and a container that holds other items passes its own consequence sentence. The typed confirmation and the Copied reveal reset each time the dialog opens, so the content stays put while it closes. Built from `ConfirmDialog` (the body in its default slot, Cancel and Delete in its `actions` slot), `Alert`, `Tooltip`, `Input` and `Button`; closed by default behind a visible danger trigger. The LabelledField variant asks for the name through a labelled `Field` + `Input` inside a medium `Dialog`, opened from an outlined `Item` row on the page, for a delete that sits in a settings form rather than a list.
platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation.guidelinesSummary: The last stop before a resource is gone for good. The user chose Delete from a row menu or a settings page and now has to see what goes with the resource, take one deliberate step to prove they mean this one, and either confirm or back out. The dialog makes the irreversible action slow on purpose: Delete stays disabled until the typed name matches.

variants.name: LabelledField
variants.summary: A short, blocking decision in a modal: an outlined `Item` row on the page names what the delete removes and holds the danger trigger, and the medium dialog it opens stacks a warning `Alert` over a labelled `Field` + `Input` asking for the exact resource name, with Delete disabled until the typed name matches. The field clears every time the dialog opens, so its content stays in place while it closes. It is the form counterpart of the default Delete dialog on the resource lists, which renders the name as a copy chip with a bare input instead of a labelled field. Built from `PageHeader`, the platform shell, `Item`, `Dialog` with its trigger, portal, overlay, content, title and close parts, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `Alert`, `Field`, `Input` and `Button`.

platform/detail/attached-resources.name: AttachedResources
platform/detail/attached-resources.title: Templates/Platform/Detail/AttachedResources
platform/detail/attached-resources.summary: An attached-resources card in a resource settings tab, here its domains: a borderless data-driven table of the addresses the resource answers on, each with its environment as the row's one medium rounded tag, its deployment policy as text, its certificate as a verified glyph and text, and a row actions menu, over a footer that counts them and adds one. Rendered in the Domains section of a resource’s Settings tab, where an environment-less domain leaves its Environment and Policy cells empty and the count reads domain or domains. Built from `Card`, `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `DropdownMenuRoot`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip` and `Button`.
platform/detail/attached-resources.guidelinesSummary: A short list of the things one resource is attached to, shown in place inside its Settings tab. Here they are its domains: the user sees every address the resource answers on, which environment, deployment policy and certificate each one uses, and can edit, delete or add one without leaving the settings page.

platform/detail/deployment-logs.name: DeploymentLogs
platform/detail/deployment-logs.title: Templates/Platform/Detail/DeploymentLogs
platform/detail/deployment-logs.summary: The deploy logs block on its own: a Logs row that reports the step count and the step in flight while the run goes, or the outcome Tag, the time and the Phased or Complete switch once it has settled; then the pipeline as an Accordion of steps, each with its status glyph, its title and sentence, its time and its own LogView, or every line as one continuous LogView in the Complete view; and a flush Progress on the bottom edge while it runs. Inside a deploy flow card it moves its controls up to the card header; on a deployment detail page it sits inside a Deployment logs card without its Logs row and progress bar. Built from Accordion, LogView, Spinner, Tag, ToggleGroup and Progress.
platform/detail/deployment-logs.guidelinesSummary: The user started a deployment and wants to know where it is, whether it went live and, when it did not, exactly which step failed and why. This block shows the pipeline as ordered steps, each with its status, its one-line outcome, its time and its own log output, so the user can follow the run as it streams, then read the full output once it settles.

variants.name: Succeeded
variants.summary: A run that went live: every step checked, the last one open, a Completed Tag with Deployed in 42s and the view switch in the Logs row, and copy on every step log.

variants.name: Failed
variants.summary: A run whose routing rules were rejected: that step is open on its error output with a Failed Tag and the reason in full, the steps behind it read Skipped, and the Logs row names the failed step beside the view switch.

variants.name: CompleteView
variants.summary: The Complete view of a finished run: every line the pipeline printed as one continuous LogView with its copy button.

variants.name: FailedCompleteView
variants.summary: The Complete view of the failed run: the lines up to the error, as one LogView, nothing from the steps that never ran.

platform/detail/details-page.name: DetailsPage
platform/detail/details-page.title: Templates/Platform/Detail/DetailsPage
platform/detail/details-page.summary: The Overview tab of a resource detail page: the platform shell with the resource breadcrumb, the full-bleed tab bar, then the column that opens on the resource summary card. The resource overview follows it with Get started for a resource made from the CLI, and the same page plots its Versions tab (the versions table) and its Build tab (repository, build configuration and token bands); the service overview ends its breadcrumb on the environment picker and follows the summary with the production checklist and the deployment topology. The summary card on its own, in its resource, service and policy shapes, is the Resource, Service and Policy variants: a subject band with the primary link and the actions, a band of labelled facts, and a state band on the canvas fill. The deployment page sits in the same shell without tabs: a status banner, the Deployment details card with its Deployment Settings band, and the Deployment logs card whose header carries the duration or the status and the Phased or Complete switch over the DeploymentLogs steps. The version page of a resource is the VersionDetail template and the deploy drawers opened from these pages are the DeployDrawer template (Templates/Platform/Create/DeployDrawer). The Deployments tab of a resource and of a service is the TableView controls row over a deployments table, scoped to the resource (the resource tab adds a small Deployments heading with Documentation and an outlined Deploy action); the service Settings tab is a variant of Templates/Platform/Edit/EditResource. Built from `PageHeader`, `PageTabs`, `SectionHeader`, `SettingsSection`, `SettingRow`, `SaveBar`, the platform shell, `Select`, `Tabs`, `TableRoot`, `EmptyState`, `InputGroupRoot`, `Card`, `DropdownMenu`, `Popover`, `Accordion`, `Flow`, `Item`, `Drawer`, `Alert`, `LogView`, `CodeBlock` and `ToggleGroup`; the summary card variants add `Button`, `IconButton`, `Tag`, `StatusIndicator`, `Avatar`, `CopyButton` and `Tooltip`.
platform/detail/details-page.guidelinesSummary: The second-level page of one resource. The user arrives from a list row or a deploy flow to answer three questions about it: where it lives and whether it is serving, what it is made of, and what to do next. The page names the resource in the breadcrumb, splits its concerns into tabs, and opens the Overview tab on one summary card of facts, followed by whatever the resource needs next: Get started for a resource made from the CLI, the production checklist and topology for a service.

variants.name: Resource
variants.summary: The summary card that opens a resource Overview tab: a subject band with the primary link and the actions, a band of labelled facts, and a state band on the canvas fill. It comes in three shapes — a resource, a service with its domains and environments, and a policy — each with its own facts and copy. Built from `Card`, `Button`, `IconButton`, `DropdownMenu`, `Popover`, `Tag`, `StatusIndicator`, `Avatar`, `CopyButton`, `Accordion`, `Alert` and `Tooltip`.

variants.name: Service
variants.summary: The service summary: the domain with its aliases in the overflow popover, the environment menu (shown below md only; from md up the breadcrumb carries the environment) and actions, the custom domains, status, service ID and creation, and the shared Deployment Settings band that expands into its policies.

variants.name: Policy
variants.summary: The policy summary: the resource it protects, a Rules shortcut and actions, then status, environment, rule count, last edit and the enabled modules, and what the policy inspects.

variants.name: ResourceVersions
variants.summary: The Versions tab of the same resource: the small Versions heading with Add Version, the controls row (Filter, search, Refresh, Download CSV, Columns) and the paginated versions table, each row with its code-set name and Latest mark, the comment, the state Tag, who built it and when, and the Open configuration or Deploy actions.

variants.name: ResourceBuild
variants.summary: The Build tab of a resource made from the CLI: the small Build heading with an outlined Deploy, the Git repository band holding the Connect your repository card, the Build configuration band with the read-only framework preset and the build and deploy commands, and the Deployment band with the API token. Editing a command raises the save bar.

variants.name: ServiceOverview
variants.summary: A service: the breadcrumb ends on its environment picker, the outlined Deploy action sits on the tab row, the summary carries its Deployment Settings band (its own environment menu shows only below md, where the breadcrumb is hidden), the production checklist expands into a drawer, and the deployment topology runs from domains to storage with Bind controls on the open Policy and Error Page slots.

variants.name: DeploymentDetail

platform/edit/attribute-editor.name: AttributeEditor
platform/edit/attribute-editor.title: Templates/Platform/Edit/AttributeEditor

platform/edit/code-editor.name: CodeEditor

platform/edit/code-editor.guidelinesSummary: The editing page of a service whose behavior lives in source code. Every field sits in a labeled section of the form column, and one save band appears only once something has changed, so the page reads as the resource's current state until the user edits it.

platform/edit/rule-builder.name: RuleBuilder
platform/edit/rule-builder.title: Templates/Platform/Edit/RuleBuilder

A resource’s Rules tab opens it as Add Rule or Edit Rule; a resource that only acts on requests opens the same drawer with a single Request phase (so no Phase section) and its own behaviors. Built from `SettingsSection`, `SettingRow`, `Drawer` and its parts, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `Field`, `Input`, `HelperText`, `Select`, `ScrollArea`, `RadioButton` choice cards, `Card`, `Separator`, `Item`, `Switch`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip` and `Button`.
platform/edit/rule-builder.guidelinesSummary: A drawer where the user writes one rule of a rules engine: when it runs (the phase), the conditions that decide whether it applies, and the ordered behaviors it performs when they match. The user composes If and Or groups of variable, operator and argument rows, picks behaviors that fit the phase, puts everything in order and saves, without leaving the resource's Rules tab.

platform/settings/settings-form.name: SettingsForm
platform/settings/settings-form.title: Templates/Platform/Settings/SettingsForm
platform/settings/settings-form.summary: A settings form and its save strategy, one variant per strategy. SaveAll, the default (a form that is one logical unit has one save): account-level settings as `Item` rows saved as one unit, the platform shell with an unpadded scroll region, the form column opening with a small page heading, topic sections each a small heading over a flush `Card` of rows, and one full-bleed sticky footer with Discard and Save; Profile is the example, with General (Full name, Email), Preferences (Timezone, Language) and Notifications (Product updates), and Full name and Email flag only after Save is pressed. SavePerCard splits a long configuration page into titled cards, each with an info `Alert`, its stacked fields and its own Save beside an optional docs `Link`. Saving one group or card disables just its own fieldset; the others stay editable. Built from `PageHeader`, `SettingRow`, `SaveBar`, the platform shell, `Card`, `Item`, `Alert`, `Label`, `Input`, `Select`, `Switch`, `Link`, `HelperText` and `Button`.
platform/settings/settings-form.guidelinesSummary: The place the user goes to change how an account or a project behaves. They scan a few topics, change one or two values, and commit them knowing exactly what the save covers. The block is one layout with three save strategies: one save for a form that is one logical unit, one save per group, or one save per card on a long configuration page. The save model follows how the page is partitioned, not the container.

Project settings is the example, with Preview Toolbar and Deployment Protection. Built from `PageHeader`, the platform shell, `Card`, `Alert`, `Label`, `Select`, `Switch`, `Link` and `Button`.

platform/states/async-submit.name: AsyncSubmit
platform/states/async-submit.title: Templates/Platform/States/AsyncSubmit
platform/states/async-submit.summary: The async counterpart of the server rejection in the FormValidation template: a deploy that runs for about half a minute, so the user walks away before it ends. The page heading carries the run status as a `Tag`; a dashed simulation panel picks the ending with a `ToggleGroup` and starts the run; below it the page shows an `EmptyState` while idle, the deployment logs card while it runs, a danger `Alert` with Edit and Redeploy over the stopped logs when it fails, and a success `Alert` with Edit, Redeploy and Open service once it is live. Progress and the outcome also ride a toast wherever the user is: one `Toast` region is mounted with the page, the Running frame shows the progress toast, and the failure (permanent) and success toasts carry Edit and Redeploy. Built from `PageHeader`, the platform shell, `Tag`, `ToggleGroup`, `Button`, `EmptyState`, `Alert`, and the deployment logs card from Templates/Platform/Create/DeploymentFlow (`Card`, `StatusIndicator`, `Accordion`, `LogView`, `Spinner`, `Progress`).
platform/states/async-submit.guidelinesSummary: A long-running action the user is free to walk away from: a deploy that runs for about half a minute and asks nothing while it does. The user's job is to start it, go on working anywhere in the console, and learn how it ended without coming back to check. The page that started the run shows its status in the heading, the logs while it runs and an inline outcome when it ends; in a full app the run lives outside the page, so its progress and its outcome also travel with the user as a toast, on success and on failure.

variants.name: Running
variants.summary: Mid-run: the progress toast reads Deploying web-app…, the heading reads Deploying, the simulation controls are disabled while Deploy shows its loading state, and the logs card streams under the Building status.

variants.name: Failed
variants.summary: The routing rules were refused: the heading reads Failed, the danger Alert carries the reason with Edit and Redeploy, the permanent failure toast carries the same two actions, and the logs card stays open on the failed step with the Phased or Complete switch.

variants.name: Succeeded
variants.summary: The run is live: the heading reads Deployed and the success Alert names the new address with Edit, Redeploy and Open service, the success toast carries Edit and Redeploy, and the logs card is gone.

platform/states/first-use.name: FirstUse
platform/states/first-use.title: Templates/Platform/States/FirstUse

The EmptyState’s icon slot shows the resource glyph; an app may draw a richer figure there. Every list that is still empty renders it with its own nouns, methods and promos. Built from Card, EmptyState, Item, Button, InputGroup, Input, CopyButton and Link.
platform/states/first-use.guidelinesSummary: What a first-level list shows before the account owns any resource of that kind. The user's job is to create the first one, so the block replaces the empty table with a short explanation and every way to get started on the same screen: the methods to create one (import, CLI, from scratch), then the promotions that shortcut it (a Catalog template, a coding agent). Every list that is still empty renders this block with its own nouns, methods and promos.

variants.name: Loading

platform/states/form-validation.name: FormValidation
platform/states/form-validation.title: Templates/Platform/States/FormValidation
platform/states/form-validation.summary: A standalone form that walks through every state a submit can land in, one story per state, on a single Create Variable page with no card around it: a heading, then `Field`s wrapping `Input`, `Select` and `Textarea` straight on the canvas in the form column, with Cancel and Create at the end of the column. Validation runs only on submit. An empty field takes the `required` state, a filled but wrong one takes `invalid`, and its helper text swaps the guidance for the message, so each field speaks in one place and there is no summary. Submit moves focus to the first field in error. A rejected request that no field owns raises an error toast with Retry and keeps the entries. A rejection a field owns, a key already in use, lands on that field and in a danger `Alert` above the fields, and never toasts. A successful save raises a success toast and clears the form. One `Toaster` is mounted with the form. While the form loads, `Skeleton` rows stand in for the fields and Create is disabled. Every story is wired: press Create with API_TOKEN as the key to get the conflict, or any other valid key to get the success state. Below md the actions stack at full width. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`. The InSync, Rejected, Reloading and Reloaded variants show where a field-scoped server rejection renders: a Create Service page whose linked origin is deleted by another user while the form is open, so the save scrolls to the Origin section and lands as a danger `Alert` under its heading with Reload origins, the Origin select takes the invalid state and the focus, and a dashed simulation panel plays the other user; never a toast, never a validation summary.
platform/states/form-validation.guidelinesSummary: Every state a submit can land in, on one create form. The user's job is to create a resource and, when something stops the save, to know exactly which control to touch and that nothing they typed was lost. The primary is a short Create Variable page (heading, four fields straight on the canvas, Cancel and Create); the variants walk it through validation, the in-flight lock, an unscoped failure, a conflict, success and loading, and then a long Create Service page where another user deletes the linked origin while the form is open, the case where a server rejection is scoped to one section.

variants.name: ValidationErrors
variants.summary: Create pressed with gaps. The empty Value and Environment take the required state, the malformed key takes the invalid state, each helper text carries its own message, and focus moves to Key.

variants.name: Submitting
variants.summary: The request is in flight. Create shows its loading state, and the fields and Cancel are disabled so the entries cannot change mid-save.

variants.name: ServerError
variants.summary: The request failed and no field owns the failure. An error Toast says what failed and carries Retry, the lock is released, and every entry stays as typed.

variants.name: Conflict
variants.summary: The server rejected a value one field owns: the key is already in use. A danger Alert above the fields says so and that the entries are kept, Key takes the invalid state with its reason and the focus, and nothing toasts.

variants.name: Saved
variants.summary: The save went through. A success Toast names the new variable and where it is available, and the form is cleared for the next entry.

variants.name: Loading
variants.summary: The form while its data loads, such as the environments it offers or the record an edit form opens with. Skeleton rows hold the layout, and Create stays disabled until the fields arrive.

variants.name: InSync
variants.summary: Where a rejected save renders: a Create Service page whose linked origin is deleted by another user while the form is open. The API rejects the save with a field-scoped error, so it lands as a danger `Alert` under the Origin section heading, the section that owns the broken reference, carrying Reload origins, while the Origin select takes the invalid state. Never a toast, never a validation summary. A dashed simulation panel above the form plays the other user. Same page anatomy as the in-page create form (Templates/Platform/Create/SinglePageCreate): the creation header, section headings over flush `Card` groups of `Item` rows, and a sticky footer, here raised with `z-10`. Built from `SectionHeader`, `SettingRow`, `SaveBar`, `GlobalHeader`, `IconButton`, `Breadcrumb`, `Avatar`, `Tag`, `Card`, `Item`, `Input`, `MultiSelect`, `Select`, `Field` with `RadioButton` choice cards, `Switch`, `NumberInput`, `Skeleton`, `Alert`, `HelperText` and `Button`.

variants.name: Rejected
variants.summary: User 2 deleted web-origin-prod and Save was pressed: the page scrolls to the Origin section, the danger Alert opens under its heading with Reload origins, and focus lands on the Origin select, which reads This origin no longer exists.

variants.name: Reloading
variants.summary: Reload origins in flight: its button shows the loading state, the Origin select gives way to a Skeleton, and Save is disabled until the list is back.

variants.name: Reloaded

platform/states/page-wires.name: PageWires

The user's job does not change while they wait: they need to see the shape of the page they asked for, so the wire draws the real page's grid with `Skeleton` bands inside the same `Card` frames, and nothing shifts when the content lands. The set covers the Home overview, the first-access Home, and the whole shell while an expired session signs out, drawn over the family of page it covers (list, detail, create form or Home).

platform/states/project-intake.name: ProjectIntake
platform/states/project-intake.title: Templates/Platform/States/ProjectIntake
platform/states/project-intake.summary: The surfaces a project passes through when it is dropped on the page: the dashed drop target that fills the page while a folder hovers over it, then the full-screen Initializing overlay that reads like the deploy logs: one row per received file as a step, its status glyph (a check once uploaded, a Spinner while it runs, a dashed ring while queued), the path and its size, advancing row by row, over the upload summary. A home page, its empty state, a creation hub and a project detail page render the drop target (the project page swaps the copy for “We build a new version of web-app, then you choose where it goes live.”); the home page, its empty state and the creation hub render Initializing over themselves. Built from `Card`, `Spinner`, Vue’s Transition and plain elements on theme tokens, with the step-row anatomy of the DeploymentLogs template.
platform/states/project-intake.guidelinesSummary: The surfaces a project passes through when the user drops it on the page. The user's job is to deploy a folder they already have without filling in a form: while a folder hovers over the page, a dashed drop target fills it and says what will happen; once it is dropped, a full-screen Initializing overlay reads like the deploy logs, one row per received file, until the upload is done and the deploy takes over.

variants.name: Initializing
variants.summary: The Initializing overlay mid-upload, held inside a layout-contained frame here so it does not cover the docs page: two files uploaded, the third running, two queued, each row a step with its status glyph, path and size.

platform/view/card-view.name: CardView
platform/view/card-view.title: Templates/Platform/View/CardView
platform/view/card-view.summary: The card form of a first-level list page, for resources people recognise by a few fields rather than compare column by column: a medium page heading with the resource name and its one-line description and the outlined medium Documentation action beside a primary large Create Application, the page's only large control, then the controls row: a `PropertyFilter` (Name, Status, Region, Requests, or free text) that grows to fill the row, a Delete button that counts the selected cards and opens a `ConfirmDialog` (the delete-with-confirmation pattern: a warning `Alert`, the selected names and an `Input` that must read delete), and `CollectionPreferences` for the page size and which fields every card shows; then `Cards` and a `Pagination`. Each card is named by a link to the resource and lists its fields as label and value pairs (the status as a `Tag`, the domain isolated in `bdi`, the request count in compact notation). Four cards a row in a wide container, down to one in a narrow one (container queries). A visible Select all items sits above the cards and the selection survives paging. All of it runs on `useCollection` in client mode: the filter, the sort and the page live in the URL, and the page size and the visible fields are saved per account in localStorage. An account with no applications keeps the heading and the controls and shows a medium `EmptyState` with a Create action; a filter that matches nothing shows a No matching applications state with Clear filters. Laid out with the theme’s `layout-boundary`, `layout-column` and `layout-section-start` utilities. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`.
platform/view/card-view.guidelinesSummary: The first-level index of one resource type, in cards. The user lands here from the sidebar to find a resource they recognise by its name and a few fields (its status, domain, region, traffic), narrow the list by those fields, open one, or select several and act on them together. One `useCollection` call holds the filter, the sort, the page, the selection across pages and the saved preferences, so the page is one heading over one band: the controls row, the cards and the pagination.

variants.name: Empty
variants.summary: An account with no applications: the heading and the controls stay, and the cards give way to a medium EmptyState with a small secondary Create Application button.

platform/view/file-browser.name: FileBrowser
platform/view/file-browser.title: Templates/Platform/View/FileBrowser
platform/view/file-browser.summary: The file browser a storage resource opens on: one flush `Card` holding a borderless `TableRoot` whose toolbar is the whole page header. The toolbar stacks the storage name beside the storage glyph, a large row of the table’s own search plus the refresh, download and columns IconButtons, then a `Breadcrumb` of the folder path beside the Add to files `SplitButton` (Upload file, Add folder). Folders sort first with a link-coloured folder glyph and open on click, a .. row leads back up once inside a folder, files take a glyph by extension, Size is muted and Last modified pairs the editor `Avatar` (named in a `Tooltip`) with the relative time; folders carry Open and files Download in their row menu, with Delete below, which opens a `ConfirmDialog` (a warning `Alert` and an `Input` that must match the name). Storage with nothing at its root renders the table’s empty slot: an `EmptyState` (This folder is empty) with a secondary Add to files split button; inside a folder the .. row always remains. Built from `Card`, `TableRoot` with `TableSearch`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `PopoverRoot`, `Switch`, `Breadcrumb`, `SplitButton`, `Avatar`, `DropdownMenuRoot` and `EmptyState`.
platform/view/file-browser.guidelinesSummary: The contents of one storage resource. The user opens a bucket to find a file, walk into a folder and back out, upload something or add a folder, and download or delete what is there. The table's toolbar is the whole page header, so the storage name, search, the folder path and Add to files all sit on the one surface the files live on.

variants.name: InsideAFolder
variants.summary: Inside a build folder: the crumb gains the folder, a .. row leads back up, and the files carry their glyph, size, editor and age.

platform/view/query-editor.name: QueryEditor
platform/view/query-editor.title: Templates/Platform/View/QueryEditor
platform/view/query-editor.summary: The query editor page placed in the platform shell: the Databases breadcrumb, then the Tables and Editor tabs, each pairing a resizable, collapsible `Sidebar` (288px at rest) with a working pane. On Editor the panel holds the query history and the pane stacks the Run query, Prettify and Templates toolbar, the editor, and the Results band over its pagination; on Tables the panel lists the tables and the pane holds the selected table with its Data and Definition switch. A database with no tables shows the Create Table empty state, and the Templates button opens the SQL quick templates drawer. Its page-level parts are `PageTabs`.
platform/view/query-editor.guidelinesSummary: The workspace of one SQL database. The user comes here to see which tables exist, read and edit a table's rows or its definition, and write and run queries against the data. Two tabs share one layout: a resizable side panel that lists things (tables, or past queries) beside a working pane that shows the one in use.

variants.name: Schema
variants.summary: The Definition view of customers: the Columns heading with Add column over a card holding the column name, its type as a Tag, and its constraints.

variants.name: EmptyDatabase
variants.summary: A database with no tables yet: the side panel says so and the working pane shows the Create Table empty state.

variants.name: Query
variants.summary: The Editor tab after the Select all query ran: the query history in the side panel, the statement in the editor, and its three rows in the Results band, switchable to JSON.

variants.name: Templates
variants.summary: The Editor tab before anything ran, with the Results band ready to execute; the Templates button opens the SQL quick templates drawer, and choosing a card loads its SQL into the editor.

variants.name: Failed
variants.summary: The rows of the selected table failed to load: the Tables tab keeps the side panel and the table toolbar, and the Data view shows a danger Alert that names the table and offers Retry.

platform/view/split-view.name: SplitView
platform/view/split-view.title: Templates/Platform/View/SplitView
platform/view/split-view.summary: The events explorer placed in the platform shell, with its navigation entry active: the controls row (Filter popover, event search, Refresh and Download CSV) over the applied filter chips, and the explorer. The explorer pairs a resizable, collapsible fields `Sidebar` (each field a column checkbox and a popover of its top values, grouped in an `Accordion` by category) with the log: the Events, Errors and Avg request time summary, the stacked volume chart whose buckets filter the period on click or drag, and the event `TableRoot`. Clicking a row opens the event document beside the log in a resizable end `Sidebar` when the explorer is wide enough, and in a `Drawer` when it is not.
platform/view/split-view.guidelinesSummary: The events explorer. The user comes here to answer what happened on their traffic: how many events, how many errors, when they spiked, and what one event looked like in full. They narrow the log by fields and time, scan the rows, and open one event beside the log without losing their place. The fields, the log and the event document are three panes of one workspace, and every filter acts on all of them at once.

variants.name: Filtered
variants.summary: Errors from the Security and Access Control sources: the Filter button counts three applied fields and each shows as a chip that reopens the popover on that field or removes it.

variants.name: Empty
variants.summary: A workspace with no traffic yet: the summary reads zero, the chart is flat and the log shows its No events yet state.

variants.name: Failed
variants.summary: The event log request failed: the fields panel stays, and the log pane shows a danger Alert that says the events did not load and offers Retry.

platform/view/table-view.name: TableView
platform/view/table-view.title: Templates/Platform/View/TableView
platform/view/table-view.summary: The canonical first-level list page: a medium page heading with the resource name and its one-line description, the outlined medium Documentation action and a primary large Create Resource, the page's only large control (on a phone they stack below the copy, each at full width), then the controls row and the resource table, laid out with the console page column and section rhythm. The whole list runs on `useCollection` in client mode: a `PropertyFilter` grows to fill the controls row and turns Name, Author, Status, Domain or free text into removable tokens (Match all or Match any, Clear filters, the match count), the sortable headers sort, the footer pages, and the filter, the sort and the page live in the URL so a filtered list can be shared. Beside the filter sit Refresh (the table’s loading state), Download CSV (every matching row) and `CollectionPreferences`, a dialog for the page size, the columns (shown, hidden and ordered; Name always shows), wrapped lines, striped rows and density, saved in localStorage. Any resource index takes this shape with its own columns and properties. The row menu's Delete opens a `ConfirmDialog` (the delete-with-confirmation pattern: a warning `Alert` and an `Input` that must match the resource name). A filter that matches nothing shows a No matching resources `EmptyState` with Clear filters inside the table; when the account has no resources left, the page keeps its heading and the controls row, and the table, without its header and footer, gives way to a flush `Card` holding only a medium `EmptyState` (the resource glyph, then a small secondary Create Resource and a small outlined Documentation on one row), so the list survives its last row being deleted. Laid out with the theme’s `layout-boundary`, `layout-column` and `layout-section-start` utilities carrying the inset, the measure and the vertical rhythm. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`.
platform/view/table-view.guidelinesSummary: The first-level index of one resource type, in rows. The user lands here from the sidebar to find a resource among many, narrow the list by its attributes, compare records column by column, and act on one: open it, deploy it, clone it, delete it, or create a new one. One `useCollection` call holds the filter, the sort, the page and the saved preferences, so the page is one heading over one band: the controls row and the table it narrows.

variants.name: Empty
variants.summary: Every resource deleted on an account that is not new: `useCollection` reports `empty` (not `no-match`), so the page keeps its heading and controls, and the table, without its header or footer, gives way to a flush Card that holds only a medium EmptyState led by the resource glyph, with a small secondary Create Resource and a small outlined Documentation button.

shells/console.name: Console
shells/console.title: Templates/Shells/Console
shells/console.summary: The application shell every signed-in page renders inside: a full-height navigation rail on the left that the user resizes by its edge and collapses from its foot (the product wordmark, the ⌘K palette with its Recents, navigation, Actions and Account groups, the navigation Menu with its grouped sections and drill-in levels, and the account menu with the theme switch, the Upgrade to Pro action and the system status at its foot) and a content zone on the right whose global header carries the breadcrumb on every level (one unlinked crumb on a first-level list, which opens on its controls row with no page heading), the search affordance, the Create button, the Agent button and the account avatar. The search is a 32px field-shaped button while the bar’s content box is at least `--container-2xl` (752px) wide and an outlined IconButton below it; below `md` the rail becomes a Drawer opened from the hamburger that leads the wordmark. First-level lists, detail pages with their tabs and Home all render inside it. Built from `PageTabs`, `Sidebar`, `Menu`, `Command`, `DropdownMenu`, `ThemeSwitcher`, `StatusIndicator`, `Avatar`, `GlobalHeader`, `Breadcrumb`, `Button`, `ButtonHighlight`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `Kbd`, `Drawer` and, per page, `Tabs`, `Select`, `Tag`, `Input` and `Card`; the page bodies here are stand-ins, the real ones are the TableView and DetailsPage templates.
shells/console.guidelinesSummary: The application shell every signed-in page renders inside. The user browses and moves laterally between modules, so the shell keeps the whole product one step away: a navigation rail on the left (wordmark, the ⌘K palette, the grouped navigation, the account menu) and a content zone on the right headed by one global header (search, Create, Agent, the avatar). Pages render only their own content in the zone; this block's page bodies are stand-ins for `platform/view/table-view` and `platform/detail/details-page`.

variants.name: DetailPage
variants.summary: A resource detail page: the breadcrumb reads Resources, the resource, then its environment, whose last crumb is a Select that searches the resource’s environments, tags each with its deployment policy and offers Add Environment at its foot; a full-bleed Tabs bar under the header carries the Overview, Deployments and Settings tabs with the outlined Deploy action, and the content scrolls beneath it.

shells/documentation.name: Documentation
shells/documentation.title: Templates/Shells/Documentation
shells/documentation.summary: The documentation shell: a `GlobalHeader` in its `content` placement (see Templates › Headers › DocsHeader), a `Sidebar` rail from `lg` carrying a `MenuRoot` of the current product’s pages and the theme switcher in its footer, the reading column scrolling inside its own `ScrollArea`, and the “On this page” outline from `xl`. The `Footer` sits INSIDE the reading column’s scroller, in its `content` placement: the bands run full bleed across the zone between the rail and the outline and open on the page boundary, like the top bar above. Below `lg` the rail leaves and the footer takes the whole width; below `md` the footer stacks. The social buttons are small and row two sizes its bands by content, so the brand mark, seven icons and the status pair share one line in a zone as narrow as this column at 1024 wide; the brand leads that row from `lg` (answered by the `lg:` utility, so it follows the breakpoint token) and moves to the signature band below it. Built from `GlobalHeader`, `Sidebar`, `MenuRoot`, `ScrollArea`, `ThemeSwitcher` and `Footer`.
shells/documentation.guidelinesSummary: The documentation shell. A reader comes to learn one task and leave, so the shell keeps the page readable and the next page close: the docs header on top, a rail of the current product's pages from `lg`, a reading column that scrolls on its own, the "On this page" outline from `xl`, and the footer inside the reading column's scroller so the bands sit between the rail and the outline.

shells/website.name: Website
shells/website.title: Templates/Shells/Website
shells/website.summary: The website shell: a sticky `GlobalHeader` in its `site` placement (see Templates › Headers › SiteHeader), one `Hero` band opening the page, every section stacked inside one framed `SectionContainer max-width="site"` separated by hatched gaps, a closing frame that draws no rule of its own, and the `Footer` in its `site` placement closing the page frame. The hero, the sections and the footer all resolve to the site measure, which is the only reason the side rules running down the page are continuous; the hairline above the footer is the mirror of the hero’s top rule, so the frame turns the corner instead of stopping at it. The footer’s social buttons are small, the brand mark leads the social row from `lg` (answered by the `lg:` utility, so it follows the breakpoint token) and moves to the signature band below it, and row two sizes its bands by content, so the row never wraps while the status pair still has room. Built from `GlobalHeader`, `Hero`, `SectionContainer`, `SectionGap`, `SectionModule`, `FrameBox`, `BigNumbers`, `TextureMaterial` and `Footer`. The full mega-menus and the navigation sheet are documented on Templates › Marketing › Shell › SiteNav.
shells/website.guidelinesSummary: The marketing shell. A visitor scans to decide whether Azion fits, so the page is one continuous frame: a sticky site header, a hero band that states the offer and the two next steps, every section stacked inside one framed container separated by hatched gaps, and the site footer closing the frame. The hero, sections and footer all resolve to the site measure, which is what keeps the side rules continuous down the page.
